stories.headline: Feral cat control helps NZ dotterel population rise from 105 to 160
stories.deck: New Zealand's critically endangered southern dotterel population has risen by 52 percent following focused predator control efforts. Intensive campaigns targeting feral cats on Stewart Island have yielded immediate gains in breeding. The population grew from 105 birds in early 2025 to an estimated 160 in April 2026. Wildlife officials stress that ongoing management of feral cats is crucial for…
stories.bodyText:
The population of New Zealand's critically endangered southern dotterel, known locally as pukunui, has risen by 52 percent in one year. The increase followed an intensive effort to control feral cats on Stewart Island, also known as Rakiura. According to a media release published on April 21 by New Zealand's Department of Conservation (DOC), an annual count of the birds at beaches across Murihiku and Southland found that their population had grown from 105 in April 2025 to an estimated 160. This is the largest yearly population increase recorded for the shorebird since focused conservation work began more than 32 years ago. The growth followed a joint winter campaign in 2025 by the Department of Conservation and non-profit group Zero Invasive Predators. The campaign targeted feral cats, which had brought the shorebird close to extinction by hunting adult birds and chicks in their mountain breeding areas.
Targeted predator control yields immediate breeding gains
Before the 2025 operation, the pukunui population had fallen sharply, dropping from 176 birds in 2020 to just 105 in early 2025. Feral cats were identified as the main cause of the decline. Wildlife managers estimated that cats killed up to 50 adult birds each year. 
The 2025 aerial control campaign used biodegradable 1080 bait to target feral cats across important nesting areas on the mountain tops of Rakiura. In the Department of Conservation's official statement, DOC Rakiura Operations Manager Jennifer Ross described the immediate benefits of reducing the number of predators during the nesting season. "After years of small gains, and more commonly, devastating losses, this is the result we needed to help save pukunui from extinction," Ross said. "We managed to reduce feral cats to very low levels in the operational area. This protected adult birds while they nested and raised their chicks on the mountain tops." Ross explained that adult males are especially at risk from feral cats because they sit on eggs overnight, when cats are actively hunting. Protecting nesting areas allowed more pairs to form and raise chicks successfully. Some pairs hatched three chicks during the season. The latest count found 91 surviving adult birds out of 97 adults previously known to be alive. It also recorded 56 newly banded young birds, one newly discovered adult and five birds without bands. Standard population estimates add five percent to account for birds that may have been missed during beach counts.
Long term threats remain on Stewart Island
Despite this record increase, wildlife officials warn that the southern dotterel remains at risk while feral cats continue to live on the island. Trail cameras placed around the edges of the areas covered by the campaign have recorded feral cats near the boundaries of the cleared zones. Cats have also been found in other breeding areas across Rakiura. Dean Whaanga, a representative of the Ngāi Tahu leadership group involved in the Predator Free Rakiura initiative, said in the Department of Conservation's release that continued efforts are important for the island's wider environment. "It's critical we continue to take action, not just for pukunui, but to uplift the mauri of Rakiura and enable other taonga species like kākāpō and tīeke to safely return," Whaanga said. Feral cats breed in the wild across Rakiura and live independently of human settlements. This means permanently removing them will require continued management across the entire island.
Ground trapping expansion to protect gains
Although no aerial predator control operation is planned for Rakiura in 2026, conservation teams are expanding ground traps and bait stations. These efforts aim to stop feral cats from returning to the cleared nesting areas. The ongoing trapping work receives support from private donations through the New Zealand Nature Fund and tourism company RealNZ. Field teams are closely tracking the movement of feral cats across the island. They want to find out how quickly the cats try to return to the high-altitude breeding areas. Genetic blood samples collected from newly banded young birds will also help researchers identify their parents and track the balance between males and females in the recovering population. The Department of Conservation's wider Pukunui Recovery Project aims to increase the southern dotterel population to at least 300 birds by 2035.

stories.headline: Bolsonaro’s party says it recognises Lula’s election win in Brazil
stories.deck: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback after trailing Flávio Bolsonaro in a first-round vote, a defeat which fired up the left on the streets and social media to secure him a fourth term in office
stories.bodyText:
Flávio Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party on Monday (October 26, 2026) recognised the outcome of Brazil’s presidential runoff, despite the candidate’s objections to the poll won by leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
Mr. Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), pulled off a dramatic comeback after trailing Mr. Bolsonaro in a first-round vote, a defeat which fired up the left on the streets and social media to secure him a fourth term in office.
In the end, Mr. Lula pulled around 4.4 million more votes than his rival on Sunday (October 25, 2026).
Mr. Bolsonaro, a right-wing senator and 45-year-old son of far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro, cried foul after polling was extended nationwide for two hours, at Mr. Lula’s request, due to transport problems in some cities.
Though Mr. Bolsonaro maintained that he would seek annulment of the presidential election, his party later distanced itself from that position and opted to accept the official vote.
“We recognise the presidential election results, as proclaimed by the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), but we believe that the concerns raised need to be sufficiently addressed within a balanced and democratic political debate,” the party said in a statement late Monday (October 26, 2026).
Flavio Bolsonaro had also requested polling stations stay open in some regions due to heavy rains, but he described the vote extension as “unacceptable” and a “dirty trick.”
While congratulations rolled in for Mr. Lula from world leaders on both sides of the political divide, Mr. Trump, an ally of the Bolsonaro family, said the election “looked terrible to me.”
“I didn’t take sides but it looked like another rigged election frankly,” he told reporters in Washington. “It looked so corrupt.”
In a video posted to social media on Monday (October 26, 2026) afternoon, Mr Bolsonaro said police had ordered him to surrender his passports, adding, “I am now prohibited from leaving the country.”
Leader of the opposition
He said the decision came from a Supreme Court justice, and was based on a comment by his U.S.-based brother Eduardo Bolsonaro, who told a U.S. podcast two days before the election that “if my brother does not win, I am in favor that he would leave the country.”
Mr. Eduardo Bolsonaro cited investigations against his brother.
Brazilian police are probing Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro for corruption over the financing of the biopic “Dark Horse” about his father.
“I never had any intention of leaving the country. I will surrender my passports and defend myself against this travesty,” Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro said.
The right-wing candidate also took up the mantle as “leadership of the opposition” in a separate statement.
Brazil’s markets tumbled nearly 17% and the dollar surged against the real in response to leftist Lula’s re-election, as investors worried about fiscal discipline.
Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro slammed Mr. Lula for “an unprecedented abuse of both political and economic power,” over a flurry of social spending announcements during the campaign.
‘Rebellious youth’
The left was triumphant after securing a historic turnaround in the vote, with thousands pouring into the streets to celebrate Mr. Lula on Sunday (October 25, 2026) night.
Lawyer Julio Canelo, 42, hailed a victory for “the entire democratic spectrum.”
“It was the result of the people mobilizing, in the streets and online,” he told AFP.
Mr. Lula’s re-energised campaign to the cry of “Never Again Bolsonaro,” urging people to go out and vote, saw the abstention rate fall from 21% to 19% in the runoff.
The proportion of spoiled and blank votes also decreased.
“I owe this victory to the rebellious youth who rose up to defend democracy,” Mr. Lula told jubilant supporters on Sunday (October 26, 2026) night.
European nations, Russia, China, India, South Africa and others congratulated Lula.
Several right-wing governments in Latin America — who are close to Trump — accepted the victory, with Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella saying even though he had backed Bolsonaro: “When the people speak at the ballot box, their will must be respected.”
Echo of father’s loss
Flavio Bolsonaro’s rejection of the results echoed his father’s refusal to acknowledge losing to Mr. Lula in the 2022 elections.
Tension over that result led to hundreds of Mr. Jair Bolsonaro’s supporters storming government buildings a week after Mr. Lula’s inauguration to demand military intervention.
Mr. Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for an attempted coup to stop Mr. Lula from taking office.
Electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques, a Bolsonaro appointee to the Supreme Court, hailed the “successful polls” and said there “were no changes” resulting from the decision to extend voting, even if it did create difficulties.

stories.headline: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ hurtling towards Andhra Pradesh coast
stories.deck: Several southern Odisha districts started receiving rain as ‘Arnab’ hurtled towards the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 27 2026
stories.bodyText:
Several southern Odisha districts started receiving rain as very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” hurtled towards Andhra Pradesh coast on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) morning.
As per India Meteorological Department, the very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” over Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved west-northwestwards with a speed of 25 kmph during past six hours, and lay-centered over the same region 300 km southeast of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 360 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 380 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha), 460 km east of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 530 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh) and 920 km west-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands) on October 27, 2026.
It is very likely to continue to move west-northwestwards till evening of October 27 and thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph by forenoon of October 28, 2026, says IMD.
Heavy to very heavy rainfall has been predicted at a few places with extremely heavy rainfall at one or two places in Gajapati, Ganjam, Rayagada, Koraput, and Malkangiri districts. (EOM)

stories.headline: Skydance offers voluntary buyouts, orders 5-day office work after Warner Bros merger
stories.deck: Skydance has implemented a strict policy requiring all employees to return to the office five days per week, reflecting a significant shift in workplace expectations. Alongside this, they are introducing a Voluntary Buyout Program aimed at optimizing their workforce. This strategic direction is in response to the recent merger with Paramount-Skydance, promoting a unified corporate culture.
stories.bodyText:
Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreitz are overhauling the company’s corporate culture and cost structure, mandating a full five-day return to the office while launching a voluntary buyout programme for employees. The directives, detailed in an internal staff memo obtained by Deadline, mark the first major operational shake-up since Skydance finalised its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery weeks ago.
Under the new policy, employees will be required to work on-site five days a week, phased in over time depending on location. The mandate aligns the broader workforce with Paramount-Skydance, which had already ended hybrid arrangements, while ending the three-day in-office model previously held at Warner Bros. Discovery. The transition will primarily affect major hubs in Los Angeles, New York, Atlanta, and London.
“We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people,” Ellison and Kreitz wrote in the memo. “We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them.”
Alongside the in-office mandate, leadership introduced a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program aimed at reducing headcount as the company tackles a daunting balance sheet. 
The merged entity is saddled with nearly $90 billion in debt amid a climate of rising interest rates. Ellison has pledged to deliver at least $2 billion in cost savings, with significant reductions expected to come from layoffs.
“As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that,” the memo stated. “To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program. Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer.”
Eligible employees are expected to receive their buyout packages in the coming days as Skydance accelerates its post-merger integration. Here's the full memo as it appeared in Deadline:
Team,
At Skydance, our goal is to build the next-generation media and entertainment company, powered by creativity and technology. We are creative-first, audience focused, tech-forward and globally scaled. And in a world of endless choice and fierce competition for attention, we don’t just want to succeed. We want to win.
To do that, we must be a strong, connected and agile company. Among our business and creative priorities, none matters more than building a strong culture, because it’s the foundation of everything we want to achieve. Winning requires us to work as one team: one company, fully aligned. That means communicating openly and collaborating efficiently across every part of the organization.
In-Person Collaboration
We believe in-person collaboration is vital to our culture and to the success of our business. Especially in a creative company like ours, the best ideas come from people in the same room, sharing perspectives, challenging one another and solving problems. Being together isn’t just about showing up. It’s about inspiring one another, learning and coaching, forming friendships and having the casual conversations that spark something great.
With that in mind, we will adopt a five-day in-office policy across all of Skydance. We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people. We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them.
While many of you are already in the office five days a week, we understand this may be a significant change to the daily routines of others. To give you time to plan and adjust, we will take a phased approach by location. You will receive ample notice before changes take effect, and we will work closely with managers to support you through the transition.
Voluntary Buyout Program
As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that. To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program. Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer.
We recognize this is a significant decision, and we want you to feel informed and supported. If this applies to you, please review your materials carefully and reach out to your leadership or HR representative with any questions. FAQs and other resources are available on the Skydance Integration or Ask Employee Connection on WBD One.
Please know we don’t take any of this lightly. We are clear about what we’re building: a company that tells the stories people around the world love, embraces new ways to connect with audiences, and leads the next era of media and entertainment. We have the talent, the creative firepower and the ambition to do it, and we will get there together.
Thank you for your commitment, and for the creativity and passion you bring to your work every day.
Best,
David and Ynon

stories.headline: Explainer | Israel election: What happens after polls close?
stories.bodyText: Israel holds a parliamentary election on Tuesday, its first since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023 that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's hold on power is at stake, with centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era, but it might take time before clear results are known. WHEN WILL WE KNOW WHO WON? It is likely this will be known within a few hours of polls closing, but it could take days or even weeks to become clear. Voting starts at 7 a.m. (0500 GMT) and ends at 10 p.m. (2000 GMT), when Israeli TV channels will air exit polls giving the first indications of the outcome. The election results will then start coming in. A clear picture may emerge quickly but if no party or group of parties has a clear parliamentary majority, it could take much longer. The final tally is expected by October 30 and official election results are formally published a week after the election, on November 4. WHY IS IT SO COMPLICATED? Elections to the 120-seat Knesset are meant to be held every four years but early elections have been frequent. .US and Israel draw up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after elections. The Knesset seats are allocated by proportional representation to national party lists, with parties needing to pass a threshold of 3.25% of the national vote to secure seats. About a dozen parties are widely thought to have a chance of crossing the threshold, so the final tally and seat allocation will take time. WHAT HAPPENS AFTER THE RESULTS ARE PUBLISHED? After the final tally is in, President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders on whom they want as prime minister and then tap the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government. That nominee has up to 42 days to form a government. No single party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, so governments are formed by a coalition of parties, and negotiations on forming a government often take weeks. Every Knesset seat counts and small parties can have a big impact by becoming kingmakers. If the nominee fails, others can get a chance to try. If no government emerges, another election is called, with the present cabinet staying on as a caretaker government.

Trump’s approval ratings slightly recover after record low last week: Report
briefs.deck: US President Donald Trump’s approval rating has increased to 32 percent, showing a small recovery. In contrast, a recent poll indicates that registered voters prefer Democrats over Republicans by 47 percent to 36 percent. As the midterm elections approach, voter enthusiasm appears to be higher among Democrats compared to Republicans. Additionally, voters’ views on economic management have…
briefs.bodyText:
US President Donald Trump’s public approval rating rose by one percentage point to 32 per cent, a slight recovery from last week’s record low, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday.
Trump’s Republican Party is fighting to keep control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections.
In the five-day nationwide poll, registered voters preferred Democrats to Republicans by 47 per cent to 36 per cent when asked which party they would back for Congress. This 11-point gap was one percentage point smaller than in the previous Reuters/Ipsos poll, which closed on October 19.
When undecided voters were asked which party they were leaning towards, the Democratic lead shrank further to nine percentage points, with 50 per cent favouring Democrats and 41 per cent Republicans.
Republicans currently hold majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump’s agenda during the last two years of his second term, Reuters reported.
The poll also pointed to a change in voters’ views on economic management. Reuters/Ipsos surveys before
the war had shown voters preferring Republicans over Democrats on the economy. In the latest poll, 37 per cent of voters said Democrats had a better approach to the economy, against 33 per cent who favoured Republicans.
Democratic voters also reported more enthusiasm about the midterms. About 46 per cent of Democrats said they were very enthusiastic about voting, compared with 30 per cent of Republicans.
Generic ballot polls show which party voters would prefer to control Congress nationwide. However, they do not show how individual states and constituencies are likely to vote, which ultimately determines control of the House and Senate. Republicans have some structural advantages in these local contests, Reuters reported.
The online Reuters/Ipsos poll surveyed 1,679 US adults, including 1,280 registered voters. The margin of error was two percentage points for all adults and three percentage points for registered voters.

briefs.headline: Can Netanyahu survive another storm? Israel votes after Oct 7, Gaza & Iran wars
briefs.bodyText:
Israel Prime Minister 
Benjamin Netanyahu
 is facing a crucial test of his political future in Tuesday's election, with voters weighing his leadership following the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks, successive wars in Gaza and with Iran, and Israel's growing international isolation, news agency Reuters reported.
Despite the mounting challenges, Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader with 19 years in office, remains a formidable political survivor. With nationalist politics firmly entrenched and the country's fragmented electoral system making coalition-building decisive, he could still emerge best placed to form the next government.
Opinion polls point to a close contest between Netanyahu's Likud party and its right-wing allies and a rival alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff and security hawk who has attracted support from both right-wing and centrist voters.
Netanyahu has made his wartime leadership and close relationship with US President 
Donald Trump
 central to his campaign. Trump has endorsed the Israeli leader, with the two countries joining forces in the war against Iran.
On Sunday, Netanyahu said Trump was prepared to act again to “finally” remove the Iranian threat, but only if he remained in power. Eisenkot, however, accused the prime minister of "relying on a campaign of fear-mongering, lies and threats," adding that Trump would work "in full cooperation with any leader chosen by the people."
Netanyahu may once again need the support of far-right leaders Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich to secure a governing majority. Both have faced sanctions from some Western countries over allegations of inciting violence against Palestinians. Meanwhile, Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party has gained ground in opinion polls.
Neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot has a clear route to power. If neither manages to assemble a coalition in Israel's 120-member parliament, Netanyahu could remain in office as caretaker prime minister until another election is held next year.
Polling stations are scheduled to remain open from 7 am to 10 pm (0500 to 2000 GMT).
The October 7 reckoning
The election comes after one of the most turbulent periods in Israel's history since its establishment in 1948. The trauma of the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks, Israel's subsequent military offensive in Gaza and deep divisions over Netanyahu's right-wing government have dominated the country's political landscape.
For many of Netanyahu's opponents, the vote is also a referendum on accountability for the security failures that preceded October 7, Israel's deadliest day.
Mali Hajaj, an education ministry employee who supports Eisenkot, said a national inquiry into the attacks was essential for the country to begin healing.
"the most important thing is the establishment of a national inquiry because that's where our healing will come from," she said.
Lisa Tortor, another voter opposed to Netanyahu, said she hoped he would leave office and a new government would begin repairing the damage to Israel's international standing and the wider Jewish community.
She said she hoped Netanyahu would go and "they can form a new government and do some of the repairing of the damage that Bibi has done for Jews all over the world and for Israel, and Israel's image."
Not all voters, however, believe the prime minister should be held responsible for the October 7 attacks. Nof Gabay, an 18-year-old Likud supporter, dismissed that criticism and backed Netanyahu's leadership during the war.
Gabay called him "the right man for the state of Israel" and said, "Netanyahu managed the war in the best possible way."
Netanyahu's wartime record under scrutiny
The election campaign has unfolded against the backdrop of years of military conflict that have reshaped Israel's security and diplomatic position.
After the October 7 attacks, in which Hamas-led militants killed 1,200 people and took another 251 hostage, Israel launched a military offensive that devastated much of Gaza. Gaza health authorities say Israeli attacks have killed 74,000 people.
Israel also dealt major blows to Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon and exchanged strikes with Iran before launching a 12-day aerial campaign against Iranian nuclear sites in 2025. The conflict escalated further this year with a joint US-Israeli war against Iran.
Netanyahu has presented his handling of these conflicts as evidence of his leadership and ability to confront Israel's security threats. His alliance with Trump has also become a key part of his pitch to voters, particularly as tensions with Iran remain central to the campaign.
Eisenkot, meanwhile, has argued that Israel's next government must ensure Iran does not acquire a military nuclear capability. He has said this could be achieved through military action or an "arrangement", including a diplomatic solution backed by the United States.
The competing positions underline how security policy remains central to the election, even as voters grapple with questions about accountability, the future of the Gaza conflict and Israel's standing abroad.
Coalition arithmetic could decide the outcome
Even if Eisenkot's alliance makes gains, forming a government could prove difficult. Like nearly all Jewish-led parties in Israel, his camp opposes the two-state solution that has underpinned decades of peace negotiations with the Palestinians.
Eisenkot has, however, criticised violence by Jewish settlers against Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. Such violence has surged since 2023, straining Israel's ties with Western countries. He has also opposed Netanyahu's far-right coalition partners, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich.
Meanwhile, dissatisfaction with Netanyahu has prompted some voters in traditional Likud strongholds to campaign against him. Others have turned away from the prime minister as he continues to fight corruption charges in a long-running criminal trial, which he denies.
The participation of Israel's Arab minority could also influence the outcome. Arab citizens of Israel, who are Palestinian by heritage, could help shift the balance in a closely contested election if turnout is high.
Although Eisenkot has ruled out partnering with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values, analysts believe they could still support a minority government led by him. Such an arrangement could offer a route to removing Netanyahu from office without formally joining his coalition.
The country's fragmented political system means that winning the most votes may not be enough. The ability to secure support from smaller parties and assemble a parliamentary majority could ultimately determine who governs Israel.
Israeli political analyst Amotz Asa-El of the Shalom Hartman Institute expects the result to be closely fought, with neither side securing a decisive mandate.
"My expectation is that we will have only a slight majority either way. No landslide," Asa-El said, according to Reuters.

briefs.headline: 17 remand prisoners escape from a sub-jail in Theni district; combing operations lead to arrest of four persons: IGP
briefs.deck: Officer in special team said that many of the accused were from Madurai, Ramanathapuram, Salem and Villupuram districts
briefs.bodyText:
In a coordinated escape bid, a total of 17 remand prisoners made their getaway from the Thekkampatti sub-jail near Andipatti in Theni district at around 11 p.m. after attacking the warders on Monday (October 26, 2026).
Following this, the district police have sounded an alert and deployed a large posse of personnel across check-posts.
Inspector General of Police (South zone) Vijayendra Bidari rushed to the spot and held an inquiry with Theni Superintendent of Police Praveen Gowtham and others.
Preliminary inquiries revealed that all the 17 inmates were locked in a cell. At around 10.30 p.m., a few among them had called the warder on duty claiming that an inmate suffered seizures (epilepsy) and sought assistance.
Believing this, the staff opened the cell and went inside, wherein the other inmates assaulted the personnel and made good their escape.
As the news spread, the police stepped in and deployed more personnel in and around the sub-jail.
The IGP said, “One of those who escaped, identified as Praveen Kumar, was secured within a few hours and three other persons were also nabbed by the teams, taking the total arrest to four.
As many as 17 special teams have been formed. Combing operations are underway to secure all the remaining accused,” he added.
Another officer in the special team told The Hindu on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) that many of the accused were from Madurai, Ramanathapuram, Salem and Villupuram districts. They were serving their terms in different criminal cases.
Public can contact 9498101570 or 9176104100 if they have any information about the prisoners who escaped.

briefs.headline: How a WhatsApp channel called ‘Lula’s Army’ became a force in Brazil election
briefs.deck: WhatsApp campaign ‘Lula’s Army’ helped mobilise voters in a closely fought runoff, as Flávio Bolsonaro challenges the outcome and Donald Trump questions the result without evidence.
briefs.bodyText:
President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won Brazil’s presidential runoff, securing a fourth non-consecutive term after a closely contested election. However, the result faces a potential legal challenge from rival Flávio Bolsonaro, while US president Donald Trump has questioned the vote, alleging that it was “rigged”.
Lula secured more than 64 million votes, defeating Bolsonaro, who received just under 60 million, by nearly 4.4 million votes. The incumbent is expected to take office on January 5, 2027, for a fourth non-consecutive term.
A key factor in Lula’s comeback was the mobilisation of voters who had abstained in the first round or backed other candidates. An additional 14.1 million voters participated in the runoff, with analysts estimating that three-quarters of these votes went to Lula.
Central to the campaign was lawmaker André Janones’ WhatsApp channel, “Lula’s Army”, which attracted nearly 11 million people and encouraged supporters to campaign on social media.
Janones adopted an aggressive, sustained digital strategy, Oliver Stuenkel, a professor of international relations at Fundação Getulio Vargas in São Paulo told news agency AP.
“He basically embraced the right’s style of aggressive politics, very intense, constant messaging,” Stuenkel said.
“The defeat in the first round jolted the Lula campaign into action. The strategy during the first round was lacklustre and saw a lot of infighting,” he added, according to AP.
Juliano Cortinhas, an international relations professor at the University of Brasília, said the digital campaign also helped pressure Meta, which owns WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook, over allegations of bias favouring Bolsonaro.
“There was ‘external interference we were suffering by major platforms’,” Cortinhas told AP. He added: “It wasn't only Meta, many others were using their algorithms to repost many images and many messages of the far-right, and they did not do the same to the left.”
Brazil’s top electoral court ruled on October 15 that Meta must ensure equal treatment of both candidates. The company subsequently said it had addressed the order.
Meanwhile, Trump questioned the result on Monday, saying, “Elections have to be indisputable and it looked very bad to me.” He added: “I thought it had a very bad look, the way it was tabulated.”
“It looked like another rigged election, frankly,” Trump said, without presenting evidence.
Flávio Bolsonaro has pledged to organise opposition to Lula and seek to nullify the results. He said, “I am going to gather elected lawmakers and senators to organize our strategy and make the lower house and the Senate our fortress against barbaric acts that are set to happen in another four years of Lula.”
However, overturning the result would require evidence of fraud affecting Lula’s 4.4 million-vote margin and approval from Brazil’s eight-member electoral court before certification on December 18.
Benjamin Gedan, director of the Stimson Center’s Latin America programme, warned, “False claims of fraud are becoming commonplace, though that does not make them any less dangerous.”

briefs.headline: 7 civilians killed in Jordan strike on Syrian militants in retaliation to church attack
briefs.bodyText:
Jordan carried out airstrikes against armed groups in southern Syria on Tuesday in retaliation for a deadly attack on a Greek Orthodox Church in the Jordanian city of Karak last week, with Syrian authorities reporting at least 7 civilian deaths.
Syria’s civil defence agency said seven people were killed in strikes across the southern provinces of Daraa and Sweida. Among them were five members of a family, including three children and a woman, who died when a strike hit a tent in rural Daraa. Three other family members were injured. Two elderly men, aged 80 and 60, were killed in separate strikes, the agency said.
Jordan’s air force said the operation killed and wounded several members of the targeted groups and destroyed multiple vehicles. However, it did not identify the groups or disclose the exact locations of the strikes.
The Syrian government said the operation was conducted without prior coordination or notification. It said authorities were investigating the incident and had opened communication channels with Jordan to discuss the matter, news agency AP reported.
Syria subsequently announced the closure of its main border crossing with Jordan.
The strikes came after a gun attack on a Greek Orthodox Church in Karak on Friday killed nine people and wounded more than two dozen others. The attack took place during a funeral in the city, about 90 km south of the Jordanian capital, Amman.
Jordanian authorities on Monday arrested three men in connection with the attack following a shootout at dawn. All three were wounded during the operation and taken into custody in Karak.
The public security directorate identified the suspects as brothers Hazzah Zaidan Mohammad and Mishal Zaidan Mohammad, and their brother-in-law Ahmad Sami Hussein. All three are Jordanian nationals.
The agency’s chief, Major General Obaidallah Abd Rabbo Al-Maayta, described the attackers as “takfiri”, a term commonly used for Sunni militants who label others as apostates. However, he said they were not linked to any organised group and acted on their own. Authorities also recovered a large cache of ammunition from the abandoned house where the men were apprehended.
Interior minister Mazen Al-Faraya attributed the attack to extremist ideology, warning that similar incidents could recur if such thinking was not addressed.
King Abdullah II had ordered authorities to respond firmly to those responsible, saying that the perpetrators would not escape punishment and that ideologies threatening national unity would not be tolerated.

stories.headline: DYFI threatens stir over Mangaluru revenue rules, ‘corruption’
stories.deck: Dakshina Kannada unit calls land conversion norms ‘unscientific’, flags problems with approvals
stories.bodyText:
Mangaluru: Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) Dakshina Kannada district unit has threatened intense protests against “unscientific” revenue regulations in Mangaluru and alleged corruption at the Taluk Office and Mangaluru Urban Development Authority (MUDA) office.
District president Manoj Vamanjoor and secretary Rizwan Harekala said Mangaluru residents were being subjected to revenue policies different from those enforced in other 
Karnataka
 districts.
“When compared to the revenue regulations in other districts across the state, there are rules that even legal experts do not understand here. These flawed regulations have become a major ordeal for common citizens. The revenue norms here have stripped away private property rights, specifically the freedom of individuals to convert a specific portion of their land for building a home or other structures, or to sell a parcel to tide over financial hardship,” stated Manoj Vamanjoor.
He said Dakshina Kannada does not permit partial land conversion from a private plot, requiring the entire landholding to undergo conversion. Plan approval must subsequently be obtained for the entire site. If only a portion is selected, he said, a penalty must be paid for the remaining land.
Vamanjoor also cited the rollback of the previously mandated Property Card, Khata complications, and the denial of land conversion and layout approvals for properties connected by footpaths or unpaved roads.
He criticised district minister UT Khader, saying promises to simplify land conversion and layout approvals had not materialised.
DYFI demanded immediate action, warning of protests over the regulations and alleged corruption.

stories.headline: Comfy seats, Wi-Fi, higher fares: Sarjapur commuters say yes to premium BMTC buses
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Commuters along Sarjapur Road want more frequent, comfortable and reliable bus services, with nearly three-fourths willing to pay a premium fare for them, according to a survey report released in Oct.
Conducted by the Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) and Save Our Sarjapur, the SORT Bengaluru–BMTC Sarjapur Mobility Survey aims to use data-driven insights to encourage greater BMTC adoption among commuters in traffic-congested areas of south-east Bengaluru. The findings assume added significance as construction of the Sarjapur Road Metro line is likely to begin within a year, potentially worsening congestion.
Of the 400 respondents surveyed, 73.1% said they would be willing to pay a premium for a corporate-style bus service offering air-conditioning, comfortable seating, Wi-Fi, fixed schedules and pre-booking.
The report lists sample issues which include a bus application that does not track buses, missing frequency, unreliability and a lack of AC buses. It also notes the missing transfer between the Bellandur/Iblur junction on ORR and Bellandur Gate on Sarjapur Road, which forces a 1-km walk. 
Other complaints were confusion over bus stops on Haralur Road.
Airport connectivity also drew strong interest. Of 382 respondents, 91.9% would consider a premium KIA bus to the airport and 82.2% from it. The report recommends a pre-booking feature and starting with one bus. It proposes pilots for Hosa Road and Haralur Road via ORR, and for Muthanallur-Dommasandra.
Mukund Kumar from Save Our Sarjapura (SOS) said: “We have presented the summary of the survey to senior officials at BMTC, who have been receptive to the idea and have expressed keenness to work with us.”
Joy VR, co-founder, Sarjapura Residents Welfare Association (SRWA), said: “Real-time tracking of buses towards Sarjapur is currently unavailable. Maintaining proper intervals between buses and introducing real-time tracking would help commuters.”

stories.headline: Karnataka SIR: Final electoral roll out on October 27; net additions remain minuscule
stories.deck: The final roll will have around 4.54 crore voters, with one crore names struck off the rolls
stories.bodyText:
After more than three months of a clean-up drive under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Karnataka’s final electoral roll will be published on October 27. The list will be uploaded on the website of the Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka.
The exercise, which began with the stated aim of ensuring that no eligible voter was excluded and no ineligible voter remained on the rolls, led to the deletion of 1.07 crore names across the State. Karnataka had 5.54 crore voters when the exercise began. The final roll will have around 4.54 crore voters, with one crore names struck off the rolls. Details on the number of ineligible voters identified, or the count of foreign citizens — another stated aim of the SIR — remain unknown so far.
During the draft roll stage, 16.39 lakh names were deleted on the ground that the voters were dead, while over seven lakh were identified as duplicate entries. Another 3.83 lakh names were deleted under the “Others” category, which is not seen in many other States that conducted the SIR. Even as the exercise comes to an end, the CEO’s office has not clearly explained what the “Others” category comprises, apart from stating that it includes people who refused to sign.
However, the largest category of deletions — 80.62 lakh names — comprised voters who had shifted residence or were not found at their addresses during the enumeration phase. Unlike those identified as dead or duplicate, these voters were not necessarily ineligible to vote. They would have had to apply through Form 6 to have their names restored to the rolls. Yet, only 7,87,534 applications for inclusion were received, a figure that also includes applications from new voters.
The scale of deletions under the SIR has not been offset by additions in any constituency across the State, with applications for inclusion falling far short of the number of names struck off the draft roll.

stories.headline: Delhi teenager’s Project Sadak logs 2,927 road complaints across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru; tracks 190 repairs
stories.deck: Inspired by an accident that left his parents injured, the 16-year-old built an AI-powered platform to report potholes and other road hazards, identify the departments responsible and track repairs.
stories.bodyText:
A pothole that threw his parents off their motorcycle when he was 13 left a lasting impression on a Vikaspuri teenager. Three years later, the 16-year-old has built Project Sadak, a citizen-led platform that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to route complaints about road hazards to the relevant government departments and follow up on repairs.
As of October 26, the platform had recorded 2,927 complaints across Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, with 190 repairs documented through photographs. Nearly 75% of the complaints concern potholes and road conditions, including uneven surfaces and speed breakers, while the rest flag issues such as broken footpaths and garbage.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru’s frontline workers battle lung, metabolic health risks
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: An occupational health screening of more than 10,000 frontline workers in Bengaluru has found a substantial burden of respiratory abnormalities and cardiometabolic risks among those routinely exposed to traffic emissions, road dust, construction pollution and other workplace hazards.
Conducted over three years by city-based Vaayu Occupational and Environmental Respiratory Illness Clinic (VEROIC), the screening found reduced lung function, overweight and obesity, elevated blood sugar and uncontrolled hypertension among workers, highlighting gaps in the detection and management of these conditions.
The screening covered 4,517 BMTC employees, 3,287 traffic police personnel, 2,169 construction workers and 379 pourakarmikas. Most participants were men aged 30 to 50, all of whom reported working more than eight hours a day.
Among workers with available lung function data, pourakarmikas recorded the highest proportion of reduced lung function, indicated by low forced vital capacity (FVC) on spirometry, at 45%. This was followed by BMTC employees (29.5%), traffic police personnel (28%) and construction workers (15%).
The screening also revealed a significant burden of cardiometabolic risks. 
Overweight or obesity was recorded in 60.7% of BMTC employees, 51.3% of traffic police personnel, 29.2% of construction workers and 62% of pourakarmikas. Blood sugar levels above 200 were recorded in 63.8%, 50%, 20% and 52.9% of the respective groups.
Uncontrolled hypertension was also prevalent, affecting 66.7% of BMTC employees, 25% of traffic police personnel, 76.9% of construction workers and 68.8% of pourakarmikas screened.
Discussing the findings at a multidisciplinary roundtable titled ‘Protecting Those Who Protect Our City’ on Monday, experts called for a shift from awareness-building to measurable public health interventions, including stronger occupational healthcare systems and better coordination among govt departments.
“We need to consider how to strengthen the occupational healthcare system, protect frontline workers and integrate these findings into existing systems. That is the direction policy should take,” said Dr Arvind BA, professor of epidemiology at Nimhans.
Dr G Gururaj, former director of Nimhans and a public health advocate, stressed the need to translate existing laws and regulations into action using available evidence. “We need to identify gaps in capacity-building and develop systems to implement interventions effectively. These interventions must also be sustainable,” he said.
Experts also flagged a lack of coordination among government departments responsible for workers’ welfare, transport and environmental protection.
“Everyone is working independently, with little coordination. If 10 people are working in 10 different directions, they are unlikely to arrive at a solution. We need to bring existing laws and systems together to ensure they work in tandem. Awareness alone will not suffice. Experts must press the government to act,” said Swetavalli Raghavan, adviser to the health department and visiting professor at IISER Thiruvananthapuram.
Dr Ravindra Mehta, founder and medical director of VAAYU Chest & Sleep Specialists, said clinical findings must translate into tangible interventions, backed by greater involvement from the authorities.
“We have been waiting for an MoU with BMTC to screen more than 5,000 workers. We regularly prepare reports, but greater involvement from the authorities is needed to ensure these findings lead to tangible improvements. Immediate measures include providing masks and educating workers about the health risks of air pollution. We also want to follow cohorts over five to 10 years, which will require sustained funding, a clear agenda and institutional support,” he said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru hit-and-run: Cook dies after being dragged 150 metres under car, 3 held
briefs.deck: A shocking road rage incident resulted in the death of Ranjit Kumar Sahu, a 25-year-old cook, in Electronics City. After a heated argument about reckless driving, he was struck and dragged nearly 150 meters by a car. The drivers, reportedly intoxicated, escaped the scene, abandoning him. While three suspects are in custody, the vehicle owner is still on the run.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: What began as a festive gathering turned into a nightmare in Electronics City after a 25-year-old cook was dragged beneath a car for nearly 150 metres following a heated road rage dispute.
Police have taken three accused into custody after launching a manhunt in connection with the fatal hit-and-run. However, the owner of the car, who was with the other accused persons at the time of the incident, is at large.
The accused are Ajay Rabidas (26), Sajal Namasudra (19) and Bijon Ray (27), all residents of Basapur and from Assam. They work as drivers for cabs and trucks. The car owner, Shyam Khoar, also from Assam, is yet to be traced. Police investigations revealed that it was Ajay Rabidas who drove the car, mowing the victim.
All the accused claimed before the cops that they were heavily intoxicated following the alcohol party and never realised what they were doing.
The victim, identified as Ranjit Kumar Sahu, worked as a cook at a paying guest (PG) accommodation in BTM Layout. Sahu had travelled to Electronics City to celebrate the Dussehra festival with his friends.
According to the complaint filed by Sahu’s friend, Nitish Kumar Mukhiya, the incident unfolded around 1:50 am on Oct 21. Mukhiya and a group of friends were crossing the main road near Pragathipura, close to Electronics City, when a white Maruti Swift Dzire driven at high speed narrowly missed hitting them.
Mukhiya waved his hand and used sign language to signal the driver to slow down and query the reckless driving. Taking offence at the gesture, the driver stopped the vehicle further down the road, made an abrupt U-turn, and returned to the spot. Four men alighted from the car, initiating a heated altercation.
Sensing trouble as the argument intensified, Mukhiya phoned Sahu, who was resting at Mukhiya’s residence about 400 metres away. Sahu quickly reached the spot, and the confrontational exchange escalated into a physical clash between both groups.
As the situation deteriorated, the car occupants decided to flee and started the engine. Sahu was standing directly in front of the vehicle. Despite seeing him, the driver accelerated forward. Sahu became trapped beneath the front portion of the car and was dragged along the road for approximately 150 metres.
The vehicle eventually came to a halt. The occupants stepped out, pulled the severely injured Sahu from under the car, dumped him near the service road, and fled the scene. Sahu, who sustained critical head, chest, and bodily injuries, was rushed to a private hospital in Madiwala. However, he succumbed to his injuries during treatment.
Deputy commissioner of police, Electronics City, M Narayana said ground-level policing helped to crack the case. “The CCTV footage we collected from the place of incident did not clearly show the car in detail. We interacted with local residents, in particular those who run all-night eateries on pavements; these interactions helped in identifying the vehicle and reaching the suspects. Finally, technical assistance also helped in solving the case,” he said.

briefs.headline: ‘Omission leads to discrimination’: Civil society group in Bengaluru flags institutional failures behind student suicides
briefs.deck: The Campaign for Rohith Act demanded effective implementation of anti-caste discrimination safeguards in all educational institutions and protection for the families and protesting students
briefs.bodyText:
The Campaign for Rohith Act, a civil society group, called for independent and time-bound investigation into three deaths — Sahil Wakode of IIT Bombay, Aditya Kumar of IIIT Ranchi, and Akilan of Tamil Nadu — students who took their lives due to alleged discrimination, at a meeting held in Bengaluru on Monday (October 26) to remember them. The Campaign also demanded effective implementation of anti-caste discrimination safeguards in all educational institutions, protection for the families and protesting students and enactment of the Rohith Act across the country, among other demands.
The panelists at the event reflected on ‘omission leads to discrimination’. Dontha Prashanth, assistant professor in economics at Azim Premji University, highlighted how despite there being a mechanism to look into alleged malpractices by students, the invigilator in the Sahil Wakode case reportedly ignored the protocol. Mr. Prashanth termed it an act of omission by the invigilator.
He also spoke about the atmosphere of intimidation that could prevent students, who witnessed alleged discrimination, from testifying.
Pointing to the social media responses following the student’s death, he spoke about how it intensified hostility towards students from marginalised castes. According to him, media coverage reinforced particular narratives originating from the institution, further alienating the students.
Mary E. John, former director of the Centre for Women’s Development Studies, pointed to how institutions are failing their students despite having an opportunity to embrace inclusion.
“In my time, IITs were ‘elite institutions’. Today, students from smaller towns are putting in hard work and securing entry to these institutions. This is a revolutionary transformation. But institutions are yet to grasp this moment of inclusion. Faculty composition doesn’t mirror the student composition and student suicides are only a tip of the iceberg,” Ms. John said.

briefs.headline: Lift protest curbs by Constitution Day or face civil disobedience, groups in Bengaluru tell Karnataka government
briefs.deck: Criticising the Congress government’s ‘double standards’, the groups pointed out that the Congress demand for the right to protest and reclaim streets in Delhi while protesters raising similar demands in Bengaluru face detention and police cases.
briefs.bodyText:
Arguing that the right to protest is essential to protecting the Constitution and democracy, civil society groups on Monday (October 26) demanded that the Karnataka government lift restrictions confining protests in Bengaluru and “free” the right to protest from Freedom Park. The groups have given the State government until November 26, Constitution Day, to revoke the order. If the restrictions are not lifted by then, they said they would launch a city-wide civil disobedience movement on November 28.
Criticising the Congress government’s “double standards”, the groups pointed out that the Congress demand for the right to protest and reclaim streets in Delhi while protesters raising similar demands in Bengaluru face detention and police cases.
The Campaign for the Right to Protest (Horatada Hakkigagi Janandolana) organised a round-table discussion at Gandhi Bhavan in Bengaluru. It was attended by historian Ramachandra Guha, besides other groups and representatives of student organisations, street vendors’ associations and labour groups.
Mr. Guha said the right to peaceful protest was supported not only by Constitutional principles but also by the legal position. He criticised the restriction of protests to Freedom Park, saying it kept public dissent away from the places where people could see and engage with it. “Ever since Freedom Park was designated the only site for protest, I have been calling it the ‘where freedom is shut away park’,” he said.
Recalling protests in Bengaluru over the decades, including demonstrations against the steel flyover project and the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), Mr. Guha said the city had gradually lost access to public spaces for dissent. He pointed to the closure of Town Hall for protests in December 2019 and said the Covid-19 pandemic further helped the government to restrict public demonstrations across the country.
Members of the campaign, such as advocate Vinay Sreenivasa and Maithreyi Krishnan, said they had been asking the State government to withdraw the 2021 order restricting protests in Bengaluru and restore the earlier 2009 order, which did not confine demonstrations to a single venue. They argued that limiting protests to Freedom Park prevented people from taking their demands directly to the authorities concerned.
The groups said protest was a way for citizens to make their concerns publicly visible and seek accountability and questioned why people demanding the right to protest in Delhi could do so while those raising the same demand in Bengaluru, barely 100 metres from the designated protest area, faced detention.
The groups also criticised the police for citing the High Court order to restrict demonstrations and said the process had shifted from “informing“ the police about a protest to seeking their permission. They argued that organisers were asked to change dates on grounds such as inadequate police security.
The campaign demands that the State government withdraw the restrictions and quash FIRs against people for protesting outside Freedom Park.
Published - October 26, 2026 08:30 pm IST

briefs.headline: Over 61,000 Form-7 applications filed by election officials in Karnataka, none cites reason
briefs.deck: Officials say they were instructed to file Form-7 applications for shifted, duplicate, underage, deceased and non-citizen voters, but auto-generated forms left the reason blank
briefs.bodyText:
At least 61,059 Form-7 applications seeking the deletion of names from Karnataka’s electoral rolls were filed by election officials themselves, with not a single application mentioning a reason for the deletion, a mandatory requirement under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.
Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs), listed as the objectors in these applications, said the system “auto-generated” the forms with their digital signatures when voters could not be reached during hearings on notices issued for no mapping or logical discrepancies, and the voters were therefore marked as “ineligible”.
This meant the same election machinery was raising objections to voters’ names and deciding on whether they should remain on the rolls. Under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 an objection that is not filed in the prescribed manner, including stating the reason, is liable to be rejected.
The officials said they had been instructed to file Form-7 applications if a voter had shifted, had a duplicate entry elsewhere, was underage, had died, or was not an Indian citizen. But as the forms were auto-generated, the reason for seeking deletion was left blank.
With no reason recorded, neither the voter nor anyone examining the electoral roll can establish why a particular name was marked for deletion or verify whether the removal was justified.
Moreover, these categories of voters (ASDDO or Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead and Others) had already been checked during the enumeration phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which led to more than 1.07 crore names being deleted from Karnataka’s draft electoral roll. Most deletions were on the grounds of voters having permanently shifted, followed by those marked as absent.
Rise after objections window
The number of Form-7 applications filed by election officials rose sharply after the claims and objections period ended on September 23, 2026. Between August 24 and September 23, only 192 such applications were received. More than 60,800 were filed after the claims and objections period, between September 24 and October 22.
The filing continued at an exceptionally high rate even as the disposal deadline approached. On October 22, the last day for disposing of claims and objections, election officials filed 10,105 Form-7 applications. Another 10,314 were filed on the previous day, October 21. On October 17 and 19, officials filed 11,132 and 11,760 applications, respectively.
Already deleted
To examine the pattern, The Hindu obtained the EPIC numbers of several voters against whom election officials had filed Form-7 applications and cross-checked their details on the Election Commission of India (ECI) portal. In all the cases checked, the names had already been deleted from the electoral roll, including those against whom applications had been filed after September 23.
This is at odds with Rule 17 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, which states that any claim or objection not lodged within the prescribed period or in the prescribed form and manner “shall be rejected by the registration officer”. It also remains unclear whether hearing notices or orders, which are mandatory before deletion, were issued in these cases, or on what grounds the names were deleted, as the relevant details had been left blank.
In the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike South district, where election officials filed the highest number of Form-7 applications, applications filed by officials outnumbered those filed by voters or third parties. Of the 17,491 applications in the district, 10,374 were filed by officials. In the Bommanahalli Assembly constituency alone, officials filed 4,095 of the 5,757 applications received.
The pattern of EROs and AEROs filing more Form-7 applications than voters or third parties was seen in at least 26 Assembly constituencies.
Karnataka’s final electoral roll is scheduled to be published on October 27. Only claims and objections received by September 23 were to be considered for the final roll. Applications filed after the deadline were to be considered only for a supplementary roll after the SIR. However, The Hindu’s sample checks found that the names of voters cited in applications filed even after the deadline had already been deleted from the roll.
It is also pertinent to note that the actual number could be higher as the number of Form-7 applications available in the consolidated Form-10 records on the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) website has consistently been lower than the figures cited in statements issued by the Chief Electoral Officer of Karnataka. The Hindu had highlighted this discrepancy in an earlier report.
Between September 24 and October 22, the CEO’s office reported 1,70,442 Form-7 applications. However, only 1,56,634 applications were available in the consolidated Form-10 records on the ECI website, leaving a gap of 13,808 applications.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru: Three arrested for murder in road rage case, fourth accused on the run
briefs.bodyText:
The Electronics City police have arrested three men for allegedly assaulting a man and running him over with a car, dragging him for around 100 metres and causing his death in a case of road rage, after he asked the driver of the accused’s car to slow down. The fourth accused, identified as Shyam Kohar, is absconding.
The arrested have been identified as Ajay Rabidas, 26, Sajal Namasudra, 19, and Bijoy Ray, 27, all natives of Assam.
The deceased, Ranjith Kumar Sahu, hailed from Bihar, the police said. He was working as a cook at a paying guest accommodation in BTM Layout.
The incident occurred near Pragathi Nagar, within the limits of Electronics City Police Station, on the night of October 21.
According to the complaint lodged by his friend, Nitish Mukhiya, Ranjith had come to Electronics City to celebrate the Dasara festival with his friends. After the celebration, he was walking with them to his brother’s house in Pragathipura, where they planned to spend the night.
While they were crossing the road, a car allegedly approached at high speed. When Ranjith signalled to the driver to slow down, the occupants of the car reportedly became angry, took a U-turn, came back and assaulted him.
Nitish alerted his friends, who arrived at the spot. An argument broke out between the two groups, during which the accused allegedly attempted to run the group over with the car.
While the others managed to move aside, the vehicle hit Ranjith.
The accused allegedly drove over his legs and dragged him for around 100 metres before abandoning him in the middle of the Hosur service road and fleeing.
Ranjith suffered severe injuries to his head, chest, right leg and other parts of his body. He was shifted to a private hospital in Madiwala for treatment but succumbed to his injuries on October 22.
The police registered a case against unidentified persons and launched an investigation. After examining CCTV footage and recording eyewitness statements, the police arrested the three accused.
Efforts are under way to trace and arrest the absconding accused, Shyam Kohar.

briefs.headline: Trust launched in Bengaluru to carry forward Kasturirangan’s legacy, support young researchers
briefs.bodyText:
In a bid to support young researchers through various initiatives, the Kasturirangan Trust was launched at an inaugural event in Bengaluru on Monday. The trust aims to carry forward the legacy of the late Krishnaswamy Kasturirangan, scientist, former Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), and former Rajya Sabha member, by supporting research, encouraging new ideas, and finding practical solutions to societal challenges.
Its work will focus on four areas: space and technology, education, sustainability, and public policy. Going forward, the trust plans to support researchers through fellowships, scholarships, and grants. It will also organise conferences, support book-writing and scientific curation, and work with institutions in India and abroad to promote research and improve public policy. In the long term, the Trust aims to build an institution dedicated to future-oriented thought, research, and problem-solving for India, according to a statement.
Sanjay Rangan, trustee of the Kasturirangan Trust, said, “Kasturirangan believed in the power of knowledge and research to address the challenges facing our country. Through this trust, we hope to carry forward his vision by bringing people and institutions together to find solutions that benefit society and support future leaders.”
As its first initiative, the Kasturirangan Fellowship 2027 will support six PhD and postdoctoral researchers whose work spans more than one of the Trust’s four focus areas and has real-world application. Each fellow will receive a one-time award of ₹4 lakh towards research costs, along with mentorship, two workshops a year to present their work, and membership in a growing peer community.
The fellowship is open to candidates who submitted their PhD thesis between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2026. In its first year, candidates must be nominated either by a group of eminent individuals who knew the late Kasturirangan or by leading universities. An open call for applications is planned in subsequent years. Nominations open on October 27 and close on December 31. The first cohort of fellows will be announced on April 25, 2027.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru Traffic Police book 539 cases in special drive against drunk driving, overspeeding
briefs.deck: The drive was carried out by traffic officers from all 53 traffic police stations to curb traffic violations and improve road safety.
briefs.bodyText:
The Bengaluru Traffic Police registered 539 cases of drunk driving and overspeeding during a five-day special enforcement drive conducted across the city from October 19 to 23.
The drive was carried out by traffic officers from all 53 traffic police stations to curb traffic violations and improve road safety.

stories.headline: Tata Motor’s Iveco takeover bid clears 80% threshold
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion (Rs 42,561 crore) acquisition of Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco has cleared the key acceptance threshold, paving the way for the Indian group to take full ownership of the company and delist the stock from Euronext Milan.
The offer secured acceptances representing 87.8% of Iveco’s shares by the close of the tender period on Monday, comfortably exceeding the 80% threshold required for the offer to become effective. The Iveco acquisition is the largest deal under Tata Group chairman N Chandrasekaran.
Tata Motors will also acquire Iveco’s 1.8% treasury stock. Treasury shares are a company’s own shares that have been repurchased and held on its balance sheet. They carry no voting rights and, under Dutch rules (although Iveco is listed in Milan, it is governed by Dutch law because it is legally incorporated in the Netherlands), cannot be tendered in the takeover offer. As a result, they are excluded from the acceptance threshold calculation, although their inclusion takes Tata Motors’ total economic interest in Iveco to 89.6%.
Having crossed the 80% threshold, Tata Motors can now move to acquire the remaining shares and take Iveco private, with the delisting expected within one to two months. 
Acceptances had stood at just 35% as of October 22.
The offer, which opened on September 4, was sweetened on October 9 when Tata Motors raised its bid to €14.40 a share from €14.10, lifting the maximum deal value to €3.91 billion from €3.8 billion (Rs 41,363 crore) first announced on July 30, 2025.
Under the original terms, the offer was conditional on securing 95% of Iveco's share capital, the standard threshold required under Dutch law for a statutory squeeze-out of minority shareholders. Treasury shares were excluded from this calculation.
That 95% threshold automatically fell to 80% after Iveco shareholders approved a so-called “back-end” resolution at an extraordinary general meeting on October 16. Under this mechanism, Tata Motors, if it secures 80% of the shares, can merge Iveco with its acquisition vehicle or transfer the company’s assets to it, achieving the same practical outcome as a traditional 95% squeeze-out.
Minority shareholders who did not tender their holdings will not retain shares in the listed company. Instead, they will be compelled to accept the same €14.40-a-share cash consideration offered during the tender process. Approval of the back-end resolution was widely seen as a sign of strong institutional support for the deal.

stories.headline: CCPA fines Britannia ₹1 lakh over '100% whole wheat bread' claim; product contains only 62% wheat
stories.deck: Britannia has also been asked to submit a compliance report within 15 days
stories.bodyText:
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹1 lakh on Britannia Industries Ltd for a misleading advertisement that claimed "100% whole wheat bread" even though the product's declared wheat content is just 62%.
In its order dated October 22, the CCPA, headed by Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare, directed the company to discontinue the advertisement with immediate effect across all print and electronic media, including social media.
Britannia has also been asked to submit a compliance report within 15 days.
The regulator took suo motu cognisance of the matter after noticing that the packaging of the product declared a wheat content of 62%, despite the "100%" claim in its advertisements.
"In the present matter, the product admittedly contains only 62% whole wheat, while the remaining 38% comprises other ingredients, including rice bran and other constituents," the order said.
It added that the claim, prefixed with "100%", was prima facie misleading as it gives the impression that the product is made entirely of whole wheat.
During the investigation, the company accepted that its "100% whole wheat bread" contained only 62% wheat flour (atta). The CCPA observed that the company had nonetheless used the claim, "blatantly deceiving consumers".
The regulator also pointed out that the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018, make no provision for using the prefix "100%" before the term "whole wheat". Falsely claiming a product to be "100% whole wheat" is therefore, misleading under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, it said.
The expression "100% whole wheat bread" clearly suggests to consumers that the product consists entirely of atta, with no additional ingredients, the CCPA said.
It noted that Britannia had, through multiple advertisements, prominently used the numerical expression "100%" as a central element of its promotional strategy.
"The use of such a precise and absolute numerical qualifier is neither incidental nor innocuous, rather, it is calculated to convey to consumers a clear and unequivocal impression and absence of any dilution or admixture," the order said.
Rejecting the company's explanation that the claims were meant merely to communicate wholesomeness, the CCPA called it "untenable" and said it could not justify a representation likely to deceive consumers.
"Accordingly, the CCPA concludes that the impugned claims constitute misleading advertisements and unfair trade practice within the meaning of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and affect consumers as a class," the order said.

briefs.headline: FDI inflows up 68% in Aug, seen topping $100bn in FY27
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Foreign direct investment has made a strong comeback with inflows rising 67.7% to $11 billion in Aug, while net inflows - after factoring in outward FDI and remittances - were pegged at $3.3 billion as against net outflows of $103 million in Aug 2025.
Based on the current trend of over $55 billion FDI inflows, on a gross basis, during April-Aug, govt officials are confident of India topping the $100-billion mark during the current financial year, a first for the country. Net inflows during the first five months of the fiscal were estimated at $19 billion during April-Aug, 68% higher than a year ago, according to the latest data released by the Reserve Bank of India. During April-Sept 2026, FDI flows in China (based on actual use) added up to Yuan 548.8 billion ($82.2 billion), which was a decline of 4.3%, according to a Chinese media report.
In India, FDI through the equity investment route shot up 87.5% during the month to nearly $7.5 billion, while reinvested earnings were flat at just under $2.2 billion. On the outflows side, repatriation was also 26% higher at $5.8 billion. There was an 11% fall in outward FDI to $1.9 billion, according to the latest data.
Govt has been seeking to boost FDI inflows and has been less bothered about outward FDI with policymakers arguing that it also reflects the growing global footprint of Indian companies, which are seeking to be part of the global value chain.
A large part of the FDI intentions announced are related to data centres, some of which have started flowing. While latest disaggregated data is unavailable, during the first quarter, services accounted for 36% of the inflows, followed by 14% in computer hardware and software.

briefs.headline: Expect rates to increase by 50bps in Dec: SBI chief
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: State Bank of India expects interest rates to rise by 50 basis points in Dec, with chairman C S Setty saying higher rates could affect discretionary consumption credit demand but were unlikely to significantly dent overall credit growth given a 7.1% growth forecast for the economy.
"Interest rates will influence the composition and quantum of credit demand, not immediately," Setty said at the Business Standard BFSI Summit. "We need to distinguish between weakening of demand and moderation of credit growth. We are coming from a phase of robust growth in credit. While discretionary consumption demand could be affected, I do not think credit for productive activities will be impacted," he said.
Setty said he did not expect system-wide concerns over credit quality, although individual borrowers could face stress from higher interest rates.
On deposits, Setty said household savings were undergoing a structural shift, with households increasingly practising asset allocation, even if they were not fully conscious of it. "There is only so much that rates can propel you in deposit mobilisation. What matters is service quality," he said, adding that the ease of moving funds from savings accounts to term deposits had improved significantly.
"The liquidity RBI has been providing and the FCNR flows will ensure that there is no rate-driven competition for deposits," he said, adding that market movements could trigger some shifts in household savings.
