briefs.headline: Blackstone’s GCC in Bengaluru anchors fresh $50bn India plan
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Blackstone has launched a global capability centre (GCC) in Bengaluru, its first outside the US, underscoring India’s growing importance to the investment firm’s global operations. The move comes as the firm looks to double its India investments to $100 billion over the next five years from about $51 billion to date.
Blackstone vice-chairman and CFO Michael Chae said the Bengaluru team would be closely integrated with the firm’s global operations and support functions spanning finance, technology, human resources, legal and compliance.
“We have about 170 employees in India, of whom around 90 are in Mumbai, our headquarters. We have been running our investment operations in Mumbai very successfully for two decades now. Bengaluru currently has about 80 employees, and that team will grow, as will our Mumbai team. They will work closely with our teams around the world to help drive our operations globally,” Chae said.
The centre is not intended to function as a standalone unit. Its expansion reflects the firm’s growing operational needs as Blackstone’s assets under management have quadrupled over the past decade to nearly $1.4 trillion.
The Bengaluru GCC is led by Susan Yung, senior MD in credit and insurance investment operations. Yung previously worked in India and was managing director at Goldman Sachs’ captive centre in Bengaluru. Blackstone has also hired senior leaders across key functions, including engineering, which will work with the firm’s global chief technology officer.
The Bengaluru team is expected to grow to 100 or more by the end of the year, Chae said.

briefs.headline: Banking to become more dependable in next decade: PM Modi
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Having focused on providing access to banking to everyone over the last 10 years, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that coming decade will focus on making it more efficient and dependable, for which cybersecurity must play a critical role.
“If we are to keep the banking system secure, its digital infrastructure must also remain protected. For this reason, we require robust data centres and empowered computing systems. We all understand that modern warfare is not waged solely with weapons. Weakening a country can also be attempted by striking at its economy. As India gains financial strength, safeguarding our banking system against cyber criminals and cyber terrorists is equally imperative. The nature of cyber threats is evolving today. We cannot counter such emerging challenges using outdated systems, obsolete training modules or legacy tools. This necessitates modern infrastructure alongside skilled human resources. It is precisely here that the role of this new Cybersecurity Training Institute becomes critically important,” he said after inaugurating RBI facilities in Bhubaneswar on Sunday.
The comments come days after SBI acknowledged a data security incident. Several other banks have also faced threats in recent months and there are several incidents of customers being duped.
In his address, PM said his govt had cleaned up Indian banks and ended the era of “phone banking”. “Today, India’s banking sector stands among the strongest in the world. Earlier, through phone banking, only those with access to a privileged family in Delhi benefited. Today, through digital banking, every household across the nation has become a beneficiary.”
Recalling former PM Rajiv Gandhi’s comment in Odisha of only 15 paise out of the Re 1 released reaching the people, Modi said: “That was one era, and this is today. Today, when one rupee leaves Delhi, the entire one rupee reaches the bank account of every beneficiary. As Nirmala ji (finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman) mentioned just now, this has been made possible solely because of the approximately 59 to 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts opened in the country.”
He said that today small entrepreneurs, artisans and street vendors and had access to loans and citizens had access to credit and debit cards, thanks to the efforts of those working in the sector, including RBI.

stories.headline: Badoni notches up his sixth First Class hundred as Delhi dominates day one
stories.deck: On a balmy Monday in Jharkhand’s capital, Badoni brought up his sixth First Class hundred and remained unbeaten on 106 to steer the visitor to 309 for five at stumps
stories.bodyText:
In his previous Ranji Trophy innings, Ayush Badoni amassed a career-best score of 217. In his previous innings against Jharkhand, in the 2024-25 season, he had racked up 205. There was an air of inevitability, then, to the 26-year-old sparkling on day one of Delhi’s Ranji Elite Group-C duel against Jharkhand at the JSCA International Stadium.
On a balmy Monday in Jharkhand’s capital, Badoni brought up his sixth First Class hundred and remained unbeaten on 106 to steer the visitor to 309 for five at stumps.
As chanceless as Badoni’s ton was, he couldn’t have helped Delhi stage a commendable recovery without the company of Sumit Mathur, who contributed 50 in an unbroken partnership of 128 for the sixth wicket. A moment of fortune fell Mathur’s way as he was called back on 36 despite holing out at long-on because Anukul Roy had overstepped.
Other than this lapse, the partnership between Badoni and Mathur struck no false note. On a pitch where all five wickets fell to the tweakers, the Delhi skipper put on a masterclass in facing spin, cutting, driving and sweeping with regal ease. He consumed just 111 deliveries to reach the three-figure milestone.
Such authority seemed a distant possibility when Delhi was reduced to 181 for five. In the first session, Priyansh Arya and Sanat Sangwan were undone by off-spinners armed with a newish ball. Priyansh was castled by Kounain Quraishi while Sangwan was bowled in identical fashion by Utkarsh Singh.
Between lunch and tea, Delhi found itself in further strife. Yash Dhull’s full-blooded drive was brilliantly snaffled by Anukul on his follow-through. Ayush Doseja’s attempted drive off Quraishi was sliced as pacer Jatin Pandey ran back from cover point and put in a last-ditch dive to complete a stunning catch.
By the close, though, Badoni had not just taken firm control, but also shown signs that another big hundred could be in store.

stories.headline: 'People say Rohit Sharma is lazy, doesn't train': Ex-coach calls him a 'ticking bomb'
stories.deck: Rohit Sharma is looking forward to participating in the 2027 ODI World Cup despite his fitness issues. Former strength and conditioning coach Soham Desai highlighted Rohit's serious hip injury from 2017, which has impacted his career. Desai emphasized the importance of regular strength training to prevent further complications with Rohit's hip.
stories.bodyText:
Rohit Sharma
 is hoping to play in the 2027 ODI World Cup, but his fitness remains a talking point as he approaches the final years of his career. At 39, the former India captain will need to maintain his form and fitness to remain in the selectors' plans for the tournament, which will be hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
Former India strength and conditioning coach Soham Desai has now spoken about the fitness challenges Rohit has faced. He revealed that the batter suffered a serious hip injury in 2017 that threatened his career and explained why regular strength training remains important for him.
‘He had a career-threatening injury in 2017’
Rohit's fitness has frequently come under scrutiny despite his long career at the highest level. Soham, however, believes people often overlook the serious injury problems the Indian batter has dealt with. Soham also questioned the criticism that Rohit is lazy and does not work hard on his fitness.
“So, people say this Rohit is lazy, mota hai (he’s fat), training nahi karta hai (doesn’t train). People need to understand this: Rohit Sharma had a career-threatening injury around his hip in 2017 – Champions Trophy jab hum log hare the Pakistan ke samne final, wo wali mein (during the Champions Trophy 2017). So he has got surgeries in his hamstring and his hip flexor and all that," Soham said while speaking to Prashant Desai on a podcast
Soham explained that Rohit's hip continues to be a weak area even years after the injury. 
He said the batter needs to follow a regular strength-training programme to reduce the risk of further problems. He also warned that missing these sessions could put Rohit in a difficult position.
“Around his hip is his weak spot. If he doesn’t train for a minimum of two strength sessions in a week, he is a red flag, he is a ticking bomb. And that is the scenario for the last seven to eight years. So if he was not working hard, if he was lazy, he wouldn’t have lasted till today," Soham said of Rohit.
Pamment backs Rohit and Kohli for 2027 World Cup
Former New Zealand assistant coach 
James Pamment
 has also backed Rohit and 
Virat Kohli
 to feature in the 2027 ODI World Cup. He believes the two senior batters have earned the right to decide when they want to retire.
Pamment spent eight years as the Mumbai Indians' fielding coach, working with Rohit during the franchise's IPL title-winning campaigns in 2019 and 2020. He said the two players should be supported if they want to play in the World Cup, with their performances ultimately determining whether they deserve a place in the team.
"Well, I think with all top players, when the time is coming towards the end of the career, it's a conversation that is always had with them. Those guys have earned the right to make the decision on when they do want to move away. If they have decided that the ODI World Cup in South Africa is a pinnacle event that they want to be at, then they should be supported to be there. Then it becomes about performance and contribution to the group.
 Now, I've never worked closely with Virat," Pamment said.
“I've watched him, obviously, very closely when I've been with the New Zealand team or with Mumbai Indians. I've watched him and to me, he's just the ultimate professional. So he's the sort of guy that I would want in my environment the whole time because he's the ultimate professional," Pamment added.
India’s upcoming New Zealand series to test the veterans
Rohit and Kohli will be seen in action in the five-match ODI series against New Zealand, starting November 4.
India last won an ODI series in New Zealand during the 2018-19 season.

stories.headline: Ballon d’Or 2026: Full list of winners, award honours and men’s and women’s rankings
stories.deck: The 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London celebrated football’s biggest stars, with Harry Kane ending England’s 25-year wait for the men’s prize and claiming the Gerd Müller Trophy. Alexia Putellas secured her third women’s Ballon d’Or, while Lamine Yamal made history with a third consecutive Kopa Trophy. Barcelona’s youth dominance and Paris Saint-Germain’s continued success also featured…
stories.bodyText:
The 70th edition of the Ballon d’Or ceremony brought the peak of footballing excellence to London’s historic Palladium Theatre. Held in honour of Sir Stanley Matthews:the legendary inaugural winner of the trophy in 1956:the gala marked the very first time the prestigious awards were presented on English soil. The evening ultimately belonged to 
Harry Kane
 and Alexia Putellas, who claimed the ultimate individual crowns amidst a night of record-breaking milestones, dominant displays from Spanish football, and historical sweeps.
Harry Kane bridges a quarter-century gap for English Football
Harry Kane claimed his maiden Men's Ballon d'Or, edging out Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona prodigy Lamine Yamal following a spectacular season for both club and country.
Kane's triumph makes him the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Men’s Ballon d'Or, succeeding Michael Owen who last lifted the trophy in 2001. By winning football's ultimate individual prize, Kane joins an elite pantheon of English icons that includes Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, and Kevin Keegan. Further down the list, Lionel Messi finished fifth in what is widely considered his final career nomination following his international retirement announcement.

Alexia Putellas reclaims her throne with record-equalling third title
In the women's category, Alexia Putellas officially reclaimed the global crown, returning to the absolute apex of the women's game ahead of her Barcelona teammate Ewa Pajor and Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw.
With this victory, Putellas captures a record-equalling third Ballon d'Or Féminin (adding to her wins in 2021 and 2022), tying her Spain teammate Aitana Bonmatí for the most titles in the history of the women's award. Crucially, while she spent the core voting period dominating with FC Barcelona, her summer move makes her the first-ever winner technically affiliated with a Women’s Super League (WSL) side, representing the London City Lionesses.

Barcelona's La Masia Academy solidifies youth stranglehold
The youth categories showcased the unmatched talent production pipeline of Barcelona's La Masia, with the club securing both the men's and women's U21 honours.
- Lamine Yamal (Men’s Young Player of the Year): Yamal made unprecedented footballing history by retaining the Kopa Trophy to win it for a third consecutive time (2024, 2025, and 2026). Since the award's inception by France Football in 2018, no other player has ever won it more than once.

Major category winners and historic milestones

- Men’s Striker of the Year (Gerd Müller Trophy) – Harry Kane (Bayern Munich / England): Kane completed a double-trophy evening by securing the top striker accolade. This marks the second time Kane has won the Gerd Müller Trophy, having previously shared the honour back in 2024.

- Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year – Cata Coll (Barcelona / Spain): Coll anchored Barcelona Femení’s defensive wall during their relentless continental trophy pursuit, keeping a record number of clean sheets.
- Men’s Coach of the Year – Luis de la Fuente (Spain): De la Fuente secured the honour seamlessly after leading La Roja to a flawless, undefeated World Cup campaign.
- Women’s Coach of the Year – Pere Romeu (Barcelona): Romeu was recognized for flawlessly maintaining Barcelona's untouchable standard of modern tactical supremacy in his debut seasons.
- Men’s Club of the Year – Paris Saint-Germain: PSG made history as the first team to win back-to-back Men’s Club of the Year awards, driven by an incredible five-trophy haul, deep squad depth, and domestic dominance.

briefs.headline: Harry Kane crowned Ballon d'Or winner, Putellas wins women's award
briefs.deck: Harry Kane is the first ‌Englishman to win the prestigious award in 25 years, after Michael Owen won ​it in 2001
briefs.bodyText:
Harry Kane completed his long quest for football's highest individual honour on Monday (October 26, 2026), with the Bayern Munich and England striker winning the Ballon d'Or after a record-breaking season that cemented his status as one of the game's greatest goalscorers.
Kane is the first Englishman to win the prestigious award in 25 years, after Michael Owen won it in 2001.
"Wow, wow, wow!" Kane said after taking the stage. "I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special. It's a good omen for me tonight. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year.
"Some world-class players in the room tonight. Congratulations to all the winners and nominees tonight and impressive showing determination and hard work can really achieve."
Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d'Or Feminin for the third time.
Kane's move to Bayern in 2023 brought the team trophies that had long eluded him. In 2025-26, he coupled that success with goalscoring numbers that made him the leading Ballon d'Or candidate.
The England captain produced the most prolific campaign of his life, scoring 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern across all competitions as the German giants completed a domestic league and cup double.
By the end of the season, Kane had established himself as Europe's leading goalscorer, turning every competition into a showcase of his finishing ability.
His influence stretched far beyond club football. As England embarked on another attempt to end decades of hurt at the World Cup, Kane once again emerged as the team's driving force.
He scored six goals during the tournament and led England to the semi-finals, combining his clinical finishing with the leadership and composure that have defined his international career.
In many ways, the award represents the culmination of a remarkable journey. Few players have experienced a career arc quite like Kane's.
Once struggling to establish himself at Tottenham Hotspur as a youngster, being sent out on numerous loans, he developed into one of the most complete centre forwards of his generation, capable of scoring every type of goal while also functioning as a playmaker.
The Ballon d'Or has often rewarded players whose success was built on flair and spectacle, but Kane's triumph is a tribute to consistency, intelligence and productivity on an exceptional scale.
Week after week, he delivered. Match after match, he decided contests. There were no prolonged slumps and few quiet nights.
His numbers were almost impossible to ignore.
Kane finished the campaign with 73 goals for club and country, a total rarely seen in the modern era. More importantly, those goals arrived in moments of genuine significance, helping Bayern collect trophies and driving England deep into the biggest tournament in the sport.
The competition for this year's award was fierce. Kylian Mbappe broke World Cup scoring records. Lamine Yamal helped Spain to World Cup glory. Yet voters ultimately chose Kane, whose excellence lasted the entire season.
At 33, Kane has finally claimed the game's highest individual honour, adding a Ballon d'Or to a legacy that already places him among football's greatest strikers as England's all-time leading marksman and their record World Cup scorer.
Putellas was presented with the women's award after winning the treble with Barcelona in the 2025-26 campaign, in addition to the Spanish Super Cup. She moved to Women's Super League side London City Lionesses in July after 14 years at Barca.

briefs.headline: IND A vs NZ A: Choudhary removes Foxcroft; New Zealand A 4 down
briefs.bodyText:
Curtis Heaphy brings up his half-century with back-to-back boundaries off Akash Deep. The New Zealand A batter first gets a thick outside edge off a full delivery outside off-stump, sending the ball racing to the third-man boundary. He then follows it up with another four to reach his fifty.
Heaphy puts up a solid fight despite losing partners at the other end. New Zealand A reach 118/5 in 30.5 overs in the second session on Day 4 and need another 195 runs to win.
WICKET! Anshul Kamboj strikes again!
India A pick up their fifth wicket as Anshul Kamboj dismisses Mitchell Hay for 12. Kamboj bowls a superb delivery that seams away from the right-hander as Hay looks to defend. The ball takes the outside edge and travels to the right of the diving wicketkeeper.
Dhruv Jurel reacts quickly and takes a good catch to complete the dismissal. Hay is unhappy with the decision and appears to question whether the ball comes off his thigh pad rather than his bat.
New Zealand A lose their fifth wicket as India A continue to tighten their grip on the match.
Mitchell Hay picks up a superb boundary off Anshul Kamboj. Kamboj bowls a delivery into his ribs, and Hay neatly tucks it towards backward square leg. The ball races to the boundary like a tracer bullet, leaving the fielder in the deep with no chance of stopping it.
New Zealand A move to 110/4 in 29.3 overs in the second session on Day 4. The hosts need another 203 runs to win.
WICKET! 
Mukesh Choudhary gave India A another breakthrough by dismissing Dean Foxcroft for 42. The New Zealand A batter attempted to pull a short delivery outside off but picked out Yash Rathod at square leg.
India A had placed three fielders to counter the pull shot, and the plan worked perfectly. Rathod, positioned closer to the batter, took a sharp catch to send Foxcroft back to the pavilion. The batter looked disappointed with his dismissal as India A claimed their fourth wicket.
New Zealand A were 91/4 in 24.4 overs during the second session on Day 4. They need another 222 runs to win.
FOUR! Curtis Heaphy played a powerful pull shot off Anshul Kamboj to collect a boundary.
Kamboj bowled short again, but this time Heaphy connected well and hit the ball with plenty of power. The fielder moved to his left and tried to stop it, but the ball burst through his hands and raced to the boundary.
New Zealand A reached 86/3 in 23.5 overs in the second session on Day 4. The hosts need another 227 runs to win.
Finally, some positive news from Lincoln! Play is set to resume after the rain interruption.
India A pacer Mukesh Choudhary is ready to bowl as the visitors look to dismiss New Zealand A quickly and seal a big win in the opening unofficial Test.
New Zealand A were 59/3 in 18.3 overs when rain stopped play. They need another 254 runs to win, while India A will look to wrap up the match with their bowlers.
Rain brings another halt to play
Play was stopped due to rain just three balls into the second session on Day 4. The umpires called for the covers as the ground staff moved quickly to protect the pitch. Everyone will be hoping the shower passes soon so the match can resume.
New Zealand A were 59/3 in 18.3 overs in their chase of 313 runs when the rain arrived. Dean Foxcroft was unbeaten on 27 off 48 balls, while Curtis Heaphy had scored 21 off 46 deliveries.
India A had declared their second innings at 516 after being bowled out for 113 in the first innings. New Zealand A had responded with 317 in their first innings and now need another 254 runs to win.
Scores: India A 113 & 516 declared; New Zealand A 317 & 59/3 (18.3 overs).
Batting: Dean Foxcroft 27*, Curtis Heaphy 21*.
4.2 overs: Nabi bowls Matthew Boyle
Auqib Nabi continued his impressive spell by dismissing Matthew Boyle for four. Nabi bowled a length delivery that moved sharply back into the batter. Boyle was caught on the back foot and beaten outside the off-stump as the ball crashed into the stumps, sending the off-stump flying.
Matthew Boyle b Auqib Nabi 4 (3 balls; 1x4)
2.6 overs: Rhys Mariu bowled by Nabi
Nabi picked up his second wicket by dismissing Rhys Mariu with a superb delivery. He bowled a full ball that swung sharply into the batter. Mariu failed to make contact, and the ball went through the gap between his bat and pad before hitting the stumps.
Rhys Mariu b Auqib Nabi 2 (10 balls)
2.1 overs: Tim Robinson given lbw
Nabi struck in his first over, trapping Tim Robinson leg-before-wicket for a duck. The delivery was full and moved towards leg-stump as Robinson tried to play a clip shot but missed. The ball hit him high on the pads, and the umpire raised his finger after an appeal. Robinson appeared unhappy with the decision as he walked back to the pavilion.
Tim Robinson lbw b Auqib Nabi 0 (5 balls)
India A's lower order continued to add valuable runs even after Rathod's dismissal. Anshul Kamboj scored 22, hitting four boundaries, before getting out.
Washington Sundar and Auqib Nabi then added 69 runs to push the visitors further ahead. Nabi contributed 38 before losing his wicket, while Sundar remained unbeaten on 51 when bad light brought an early end to the day's play.
New Zealand A also missed the services of injured seamer Simon Keene, who had taken five wickets in India's first innings. Zak Gibson was their most successful bowler on Day 3, finishing with two wickets for 58 runs.
Padikkal's outstanding innings came to an end at 199 in a controversial manner. He was given out caught behind down the leg-side, just one run short of a double century.
The batter appeared to question the decision, gesturing towards the umpire as he seemed to indicate that there was a gap between his bat and the ball.
His dismissal ended a superb innings that had put India A in a strong position after their difficult start to the match.
Yash Rathod joined Padikkal and ensured that India A did not lose their momentum. He attacked Lennox and also hit Kristian Clarke for two boundaries and a six.
Rathod reached his half-century in just 54 balls, supporting Padikkal as India A extended their advantage. He eventually scored 66 before getting out after Tea.
If this was forwarded to you, subscribe for direct delivery and discover more newsletters.
India A resumed Day 3 at 56, with Padikkal batting alongside Sai Sudharsan, who was unbeaten on 39 overnight. The two left-handers put the New Zealand A bowlers under pressure with positive batting and helped India A move ahead in the match.
Sudharsan scored a valuable 91 before New Zealand A dismissed him with a short-ball plan. Padikkal continued to attack and reached his 12th first-class century by hitting Jayden Lennox for a six.
The partnership gave India A control of the game. However, Sudharsan's dismissal and the departure of captain Dhruv Jurel briefly gave the hosts a chance to fight back.

briefs.headline: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or, becomes 1st player to claim two awards in one night
briefs.deck: Harry Kane made history at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win football’s most prestigious individual honour. The Bayern Munich striker also claimed the Gerd Müller Trophy, completing a historic double after scoring 73 goals for club and country. His extraordinary campaign marks a defining moment in his career and English football history.
briefs.bodyText:
Harry Kane has spent years chasing the biggest prizes in football, and his latest achievement has taken him somewhere no player has reached before. The Bayern Munich striker has won the 2026 Ballon d’Or, ending a 25-year wait for an English winner, while also claiming the Gerd Müller Trophy at the same ceremony. His 73 goals for club and country made the case, with the resulting double giving an extraordinary season an equally historic finish.
Kane ends England’s 25-year Ballon d’Or wait
The Leytonstone-born forward becomes the fifth Englishman to win the men’s Ballon d’Or, following Sir Stanley Matthews in 1956, Sir Bobby Charlton in 1966, Kevin Keegan in 1978 and 1979, and Michael Owen in 2001. Kane’s seventh Ballon d’Or nomination proved to be the charm, with the Bayern Munich striker finally claiming the coveted prize after years of falling short amid a lack of major team trophies. His victory ends England’s 25-year wait for a winner and makes him the first player to collect the award as a Bayern Munich player.
Matthews was the inaugural winner when the prize was introduced in 1956, while Keegan remains the only Englishman to win it twice and the only one to claim it in consecutive years. Keegan also previously held the distinction of being the only English winner playing for a foreign club, having collected both awards while representing Hamburg in Germany.
Kane’s 2026 triumph follows a season in which he scored 73 goals across 65 competitive appearances for Bayern and England, alongside eight assists. He finished with the second-highest single-season goal tally by a player in the 21st century, averaging more than a goal per appearance across the campaign.
The final men’s Ballon d’Or rankings placed Kylian Mbappé second and Lamine Yamal third, while Lionel Messi ended the night in fifth.
The final top 10:
- Harry Kane
- Kylian Mbappé
- Lamine Yamal
- Rodri
- Lionel Messi
- Khvicha Kvaratskhelia
- Ousmane Dembélé
- Erling Haaland
- Michael Olise
- Fabián Ruiz
Kane was joined in the winners’ spotlight by his female counterpart, Alexia Putellas, who won the 2026 Ballon d’Or Féminin. The Barcelona legend claimed the women’s prize for a record-equalling third time, following her victories in 2021 and 2022, keeping the award in Spanish hands for a sixth consecutive year.
Putellas was rewarded for a spectacular 2025–26 campaign with Barcelona Femení, captaining the club to a historic quadruple that included the UEFA Women’s Champions League, before moving to London City Lionesses.
Bayern’s 61 goals explain the scale of his season
Kane’s club campaign supplied the largest share of his remarkable total, with 61 goals and seven assists across 51 appearances for Bayern in all competitions. His Bundesliga record was particularly striking: he scored 36 times in 31 appearances, including 26 starts, at a rate of one goal every 66.1 minutes.
He carried that finishing into Europe, scoring 14 goals in 13 Champions League appearances as Bayern reached the semi-finals, while also contributing two assists in the competition. His domestic cup campaign proved even more prolific, with 10 goals in six DFB-Pokal appearances as Bayern secured their 21st triumph in the competition, including a hat-trick from Kane in the final against Stuttgart.
Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane at the Golden Boot award ceremony for Europe's top scorer, in Munich, Germany, Wednesday, Aug. 19, 2026. (Christoph Lother/dpa via AP)
He also scored once in one appearance in the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup, completing a season in which his goals came across every major competition Bayern contested. His combined rate of one goal or assist every 59 minutes reflected how frequently he influenced matches, whether by finishing moves himself or creating opportunities for teammates.
The season also brought Kane a second European Golden Shoe and the Bundesliga’s Torjägerkanone for the third consecutive campaign, reinforcing his position as the division’s leading scorer. His individual recognition now extends beyond those domestic honours, with the Ballon d’Or placing him at the top of world football’s annual individual rankings.
The Gerd Müller Trophy makes it a historic double
Kane’s second award on the night was the Gerd Müller Trophy, which recognises the leading goalscorer across club and international football during a European season. Introduced in 2021 as the Striker of the Year award, it was renamed in 2022 to honour the legendary German forward, who died in 2021.
Kane had already won the trophy in 2024 and collected it again in 2026, but adding the main Ballon d’Or created a first in the ceremony’s history. No player had previously won two individual awards during the same Ballon d’Or gala, although organisers had confirmed that the rules permitted multiple honours because each award is decided through a separate voting process.
The possibility had been there, but Kane’s 73-goal campaign turned it into reality, making him the first player to claim both prizes at one ceremony. His achievement also gives the Gerd Müller Trophy a different significance, moving beyond recognition for goals alone to accompany the sport’s most prestigious individual award.
England’s record scorer is closing in on another landmark
Kane’s contribution to England’s season further strengthened his case, with 12 international goals taking his career tally for the national team to 91. He became England’s record goalscorer in 2024, and his latest run has brought the century mark within reach.
Six of those goals came at the 2026 World Cup, where three were match-winners and Kane overtook Gary Lineker to become England’s leading scorer in World Cup finals. Lineker himself had been nominated for the Ballon d’Or five times, adding another historical connection to Kane’s latest achievement.
England's Harry Kane (9) celebrates after scoring a goal during the World Cup Group L soccer match between England and Croatia in Arlington, Texas, near Dallas, Wednesday, June 17, 2026. (AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)
During the period used to assess the Striker of the Year award, Kane scored for England every 97.7 minutes. Since September 2025, he has also accounted for 32.4 per cent of England’s goals in matches he played, underlining how central he remains to the national side’s attack.
At 33, Kane has now collected the Ballon d’Or, the Gerd Müller Trophy, another European Golden Shoe and a third consecutive Bundesliga scoring title in a season that has reshaped his place in football history. England’s wait for another winner is over, and no player has ever left a Ballon d’Or ceremony with the same two individual honours that Kane has claimed.

briefs.headline: De la Fuente wins men's Ballon d'Or coach of the year; Pere Romeu bags women’s award
briefs.bodyText:
Luis de la Fuente won the Ballon d'Or for men's coach of the year on Monday (October 26, 2026) after leading Spain to World Cup glory.
"Teamwork makes us invincible. This is a great honour," de la Fuente said after collecting the award at a ceremony in London.
"The secret is to work with very generous players that put the team first. We've got such an amazing pool of talent, the best in the world, so as a coach I have such a great amount of talent to work with. So this is their success," he added.
In an age of coaches who were previously star players, 65-year-old de la Fuente stands out as a technician who worked his way up through the national coaching ranks in Spain.
After a solid career as a player led to an undistinguished stint in club coaching, he was flicking through the sports pages in 2013 when he saw an advert placed by the Spanish Football Federation for a youth team coach.
He applied, got the job with Spain's Under-19s, and 13 years later, some of the players from that squad were part of the teams he has led to victory in the Nations League, Euro 2024 and then the World Cup.
De la Fuente insisted from the start in the United States this summer that he had the strongest squad in the tournament, even when they stumbled to a goalless draw against World Cup debutants Cape Verde in their opening match.
They built momentum with each match and dispatched one of the pre-tournament favourites, France, in a clinical 2-0 win in the semi-final.
In a tight final against Lionel Messi's Argentina in New Jersey, de la Fuente's men kept their cool in the face of muscular tactics from the opposition and Ferran Torres smashed in the winning goal for a 1-0 victory.
The women's coaching award was awarded to Barcelona's Pere Romeu for masterminding a season in which they won the Spanish league, Spanish cup, Super Cup and Champions League.

briefs.headline: Lamine Yamal sets Ballon d’Or record by completing historic Kopa Trophy hat-trick
briefs.deck: Lamine Yamal made history at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, winning the Kopa Trophy for a third consecutive year. The 19-year-old Barcelona forward became the first player to achieve the feat since the award’s introduction in 2018. His latest triumph follows an impressive season with Barcelona and Spain, further cementing his status among football’s brightest young talents.
briefs.bodyText:
Lamine Yamal has already spent much of his teenage career collecting milestones that seemed difficult enough to achieve once, but the Barcelona forward has now done something nobody had managed before. At 19, he has won the Kopa Trophy for a third consecutive year, completing a historic hat-trick at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London while remaining a contender for football’s biggest individual prize.
Yamal makes Kopa Trophy history in London
Yamal was named the winner of the 2026 Kopa Trophy, awarded to the world’s best male player under the age of 21, at the 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony on October 26 in London. Having claimed the honour in 2024 and 2025, the Spain international became the first player to win it three years in succession.
Since France Football introduced the Kopa Trophy in 2018 to honor the best player in the world under the age of 21, no other individual has ever won it more than once.
The Barcelona forward, who first broke into the senior side in 2023, had already established himself among the most closely watched young footballers in the world. Winning the award for the first time at 17, retaining it at 18 and now completing the hat-trick at 19 has given his rapid rise another landmark achievement.
Yamal came out ahead of a field that included Barcelona team-mate Pau Cubarsí, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Yan Diomandé, among other nominees. His performances across the previous season helped persuade the voting jury to recognise him again, with his attacking influence remaining central to his reputation.
Lamine Yamal of Spain is hugged by president of FC Barcelona Joan Laporta as they attend the Ballon d'Or ceremony at the London Palladium Theatre in London, England, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026 . (AP Photo/Kin Cheung)
The award also continued Spain’s remarkable recent record in the category. Spanish players have won five of the last six editions, with Yamal responsible for three consecutive victories after earlier wins by Pedri in 2021 and Gavi in 2022.
The season behind Yamal’s third award
Yamal’s latest Kopa Trophy followed a productive 2025–26 campaign with Barcelona and Spain, during which he contributed 25 goals and 20 assists across 57 appearances in all competitions.
The winger helped Barcelona win LaLiga and the Spanish Super Cup, while his international campaign brought further recognition after Spain’s triumph at the 2026 World Cup. His season statistics included six yellow cards and no red cards, alongside three collective titles.
Soccer Football - UEFA Champions League - Galatasaray v FC Barcelona - Rams Park, Istanbul, Turkey - October 13, 2026 FC Barcelona's Lamine Yamal celebrates their third goal, scored by Anthony Gordon REUTERS/Dilara Senkaya
His style has remained a major part of his appeal, combining close control and electric dribbling with the ability to create chances and contribute goals. Those qualities have made him an important attacking presence for Barcelona despite his age, while his performances have continued to attract attention beyond Spain.
The Kopa Trophy recognises the best young player in world football, but Yamal’s presence among the nominees for the senior Men’s Ballon d’Or also placed him in contention for the ceremony’s biggest individual honour. He was one of several players nominated in more than one category, alongside compatriots Cata Coll and Cubarsí.
How Yamal compares with previous winners
The Kopa Trophy was first awarded in 2018, when Kylian Mbappé won the inaugural edition, followed by Matthijs de Ligt in 2019. No award was presented in 2020, before Pedri collected the honour in 2021 and Gavi won in 2022.
Jude Bellingham took the prize in 2023, before Yamal began his run of three consecutive victories in 2024. His wins in 2025 and 2026 have now extended that sequence beyond anything previously achieved in the award’s history.
Spain's Lamine Yamal responds to a question during a news conference Monday, July 13, 2026, in Arlington, Texas, ahead of the team's World Cup semifinal soccer match against France. (AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)
Yamal’s latest victory also comes after he became a World Cup winner with Spain, adding another major team achievement to a career that has advanced unusually quickly. At 19, he has already secured three Kopa Trophies, domestic honours with Barcelona and a place among the candidates for the Ballon d’Or.
His third consecutive win confirms that the young Barcelona forward has moved beyond being a promising newcomer, with his performances now judged against the highest expectations in the game. The challenge ahead is to sustain that level as his career develops, rather than simply add another record to a collection already growing at an extraordinary pace.

briefs.headline: Why Lionel Messi has decided not to attend the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony
briefs.deck: Lionel Messi’s absence from the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London has raised questions as Kylian Mbappé, Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal await the results. Despite earning his 17th nomination, Messi reportedly skipped the event amid Inter Miami commitments and a demanding travel schedule. Speculation about him presenting the trophy also proved unfounded, with no official confirmation of the…
briefs.bodyText:
The biggest names in football have arrived at London’s Palladium for the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, but one familiar face is conspicuously absent from the occasion. Kylian Mbappé, Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal have taken their seats after the red-carpet arrivals, while 
Lionel Messi
, a nominee for the award for the 17th time in his career, is nowhere to be seen. His absence has raised an obvious question, particularly after reports suggested he could play a special role in the ceremony.
Messi misses the ceremony as the final countdown begins
The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony was due to begin earlier on Monday, October 26, but heavy London traffic pushed the main event at the Palladium back by 30 minutes. The red-carpet arrivals have since wrapped up, with Mbappé drawing attention in a custom suede tuxedo, while Kane and teenage sensation Yamal have also arrived ahead of the announcement.
Other prominent attendees include Alexia Putellas, Ousmane Dembélé and former football great Andriy Shevchenko, but Messi will not be joining them in London. The Argentine remains among the 30 nominees and has secured a place in the top 10 of this year’s rankings, making his absence particularly noticeable as the ceremony gets underway.
Messi has won the Ballon d’Or a record eight times, most recently in 2023, and has been named among the top 10 finalists for the 2026 award following another impressive campaign with Inter Miami and Argentina. 
However, his decision to remain in the United States appears to reflect his demanding schedule rather than any lack of interest in football’s most prestigious individual honour.
A demanding schedule leaves little room for another flight
Messi had only recently returned to the United States after travelling to Oviedo, Spain, to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports. Another transatlantic journey to London would have meant further travel with little time to recover, particularly with Inter Miami approaching an important stage of its MLS campaign.
Lionel Messi becomes the first footballer to individually win Spain’s prestigious Princess of Asturias Award, recognising sporting excellence and philanthropy/ Image: Instagram
Inter Miami played the New York Red Bulls on October 24 and are scheduled to face FC Cincinnati on October 28, leaving Messi and the coaching staff focused on preparation, rest and recovery. The upcoming fixture carries added importance as the club works towards the MLS play-offs, with Messi still central to its hopes of finishing the season strongly
He also has responsibilities away from the senior team, with the second edition of the Messi Cup taking place in South Florida from October 25 to November 1. The international under-16 youth tournament is being hosted at Inter Miami’s stadium, and Messi is involved in its organisation, giving him another commitment during the same week as the Ballon d’Or ceremony
The reported presenter role never materialised
Speculation about Messi’s possible attendance gathered momentum after reports attributed to independent journalist Juan Jesus suggested that he would attend the ceremony with his family and personally present the trophy to this year’s winner. The idea quickly attracted attention because Messi remains a nominee himself, creating an amusing possibility if he were to win his ninth Ballon d’Or.
However, neither Messi’s attendance, his family’s reported presence nor the proposed presenter role had been officially confirmed by France Football or UEFA. Subsequent reporting also indicated that Messi had not received an invitation to present a trophy, with transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano among those reporting that he would not be performing that role.
The suggestion that Messi might hand the award to Yamal had also fuelled talk of a symbolic passing of the torch, particularly because the two share a remarkable connection through a 2007 photograph taken for a charity calendar. In the image, a 20-year-old Messi posed with a five-month-old Yamal, long before the youngster emerged as one of football’s leading prospects.
That story would have made for a memorable ceremony, but the presenter rumours were never established as fact, and Messi’s absence means the anticipated moment will not take place as reported.
A 17th nomination adds another chapter to Messi’s record
Messi’s absence does not diminish the significance of his return to the shortlist after missing out on nominations in the previous two editions. His 2026 campaign included helping Argentina reach the World Cup final, scoring eight goals during the tournament, while he also continued to produce for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.
The nomination takes his total to 17, spanning two decades from his first inclusion in 2006, and leaves him second behind Cristiano Ronaldo, who has received 18 nominations. Messi remains the only player to have won the award while representing a club outside Europe, and his four consecutive victories between 2009 and 2012 remain unmatched.
Whether he adds a ninth trophy or watches the outcome from home, Messi’s place among the most decorated players in the award’s history is already secure. For now, though, the London ceremony will proceed without him, as the remaining contenders wait to discover who takes home the 2026 prize.

briefs.headline: Nobody on the outside can judge the length of my spells: Shami
briefs.deck: The 36-year-old hasn’t played for India since the ICC Champions Trophy in March 2025. While he continues to turn up for Bengal in the domestic circuit, the persistent absence from the national set-up has raised questions about his fitness standards. The experienced quick offered his response after being ignored for the tour of New Zealand, and says that he is enjoying playing for his State team…
briefs.bodyText:
It was a warm Tuesday afternoon at the Airforce Complex Ground in Palam. As soon as Bengal wrapped up a 60-run victory over Services on the stroke of what should have been the scheduled tea interval in the second round of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy, the journalists present, a significant number for a domestic encounter at a quaint venue in the national capital, hovered outside the winning team’s dressing room. An interaction with Mohammed Shami was unanimously sought.
Shami hadn’t even taken part in the Ranji fixture, but he was clearly the star attraction at the culmination of the game. Two days before the commencement of the encounter, the veteran pacer’s name had again been omitted from India’s squads for the ODI and Test series against New Zealand next month.
It has been a theme for the last year. Shami has been keen to prove his detractors wrong and allay doubts over his fitness by playing regularly for Bengal – he played in seven of nine matches in the State’s Ranji semifinal exit last season – in the domestic circuit, but the wise men of Indian cricket have repeatedly looked in a different direction.
His last assignment for the country was the ICC Champions Trophy in March 2025. He had returned to the Indian set-up just ahead of the tournament after a lengthy lay-off due to a knee injury and ankle surgery following the 2023 ODI World Cup. Over the course of the eight-team Champions Trophy, where spearhead Jasprit Bumrah was missing in action because of a lower back injury, Shami stepped up ably, scalping nine victims in five matches in India’s undefeated march to glory.
Yet, Shami’s yearning for a return to the bright lights of international cricket hasn’t materialised.
Whether that will change in whatever is remaining of his career is uncertain. Regardless, Shami’s reputation as one of India’s finest fast bowlers cannot be taken away. Particularly when he was part of the pace attack also featuring Bumrah, Ishant Sharma and Umesh Yadav under Virat Kohli’s captaincy, there was no let-up for the batter facing. Shami, never mind his fondness for a sumptuous plate of biryani, would charge in all day long and release the ball with a perfectly upright seam to make it jag at his command. He went on to produce many great spells, as 229 wickets in 64 Tests and 206 scalps in 108 ODIs testify.
During the course of the media interaction in Palam, he set the record straight on his fitness, responded to his omission for the tour of New Zealand, the motivation to play for Bengal and more. Excerpts:
You had trained on the day before the Bengal-Services game. The Bengal captain and coach said that you were fit and resting. What was the reasoning behind you opting not to play the match?
I trained on day three and four of the game too. You could see the condition of the pitch, right? There was no point in playing on this wicket and bowling two to four overs. It was better that the youngsters got a run. The more they play, the more experience they will get. My motive is that when the team requires me, I play. I don’t think there was really a need here. I can’t play as a batter.
You have been playing domestic cricket regularly. Yet, you are not part of the touring party to New Zealand. How disappointing is it to have been overlooked for the series?
It was not about disappointment. I played (almost) all the matches last season as well. My motive is to play as much as I can in the upcoming tournaments. Nobody knows when anybody will be needed. For me, it is good even for Indian Premier League (IPL) preparation if I keep playing domestic cricket. As long as I play a lot of matches, my rhythm will be good. If I am with the team, the atmosphere will be good. These are the things that I try to do.
Your record in international cricket is proven. Skill-wise, do you still consider yourself one of the best in Indian cricket right now?
I can’t praise myself. That is something that you all will have to be asked. But I try to ensure that whoever I am playing for, I tick the boxes required and fulfil my responsibility. I try to ensure that my effort is 100% and the team’s needs are fulfilled. I don’t think of anything more than this.
You have played a lot of cricket with Bhuvneshwar Kumar. He has made a comeback to the T20I team. Does it offer encouragement that your performances in domestic cricket will also be rewarded?
I don’t know what will happen or not happen. But there can’t be anything better for any player than the fact that the domestic season has started. This is the best platform for any player to get into rhythm. Whoever is available, whether senior or junior, should look to make the competition tough for the opponent (in domestic cricket).
How happy are you for Bhuvneshwar to have earned a recall?
The way he has performed, he should have been there in the Indian team much earlier.
There has been talk that you haven’t been able to bowl long spells for Bengal, and that you have needed frequent breaks off the field. What would you like to say to that?
How can anyone from the outside judge whether I am bowling long spells? It is dependent on the demands of the team. It is not like I will keep bowling over after over. On a wicket like this, for example, how can you plan to have a fast bowler bowl five or ten overs on the trot? If it is uncomfortable for a batter, the fast bowler will bowl. If we think a spinner will take the wickets, he will bowl more. This depends entirely on the game situation and pitch conditions. That is the captain’s call.
By the way, I bowled for one-and-a-half hours today. There was no issue.
You have had your peak. Is your age a barrier now?
I am still at my peak. There is no point in not saying what I think is right. Regardless of how old I am, I feel I am at my peak.
You were instrumental in India reaching the 2023 ODI World Cup final. The next World Cup is in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, and just a year away. How keen are you to keep pushing yourself with that tournament in mind?
I do not think that far ahead. You never know what will happen in life. You don’t know who will score runs or take wickets. There is no point thinking that far ahead. Just keep playing the matches. Just keep improving. I always say that my focus should be on my skill and my fitness. I don’t want to take on any load by thinking about the future. I am getting to play domestic cricket right now. There is a lot of time (for the 2027 ODI World Cup). I am just playing.
There has been a change in the selection panel recently. Ajit Agarkar has left his role. Has there been any communication with the selectors after that?
I am not with the Indian team. I am not contracted. Why will anybody talk to me right now?
How much are you enjoying this phase of playing domestic cricket for Bengal?
This is the team that has given me a name. All these cameras and questions are because of this team. And whenever I end my career, it will be with this team. The stage or level does not matter. You should have loyalty and work hard. I am doing that. Only that is in my control. The rest isn’t in my control. That is how I think.
You say that the 2027 World Cup is some time away. But how much hope do you realistically have of playing for India again?
Why would I give up hope? Hope should always be there. I say this for any profession. You should always have a goal. Even when we play in the Ranji Trophy, it is to win the title for the State. Goals should always be there. I don’t deny that.

briefs.headline: Ballon d’Or 2026 leaked: Kane, Mbappé and Yamal all declared winners
briefs.deck: The 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London was thrown into confusion after articles declaring Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal winners reportedly appeared on the award’s official website. The pages sparked speculation about a possible result leak before being removed. With all three among the leading contenders, fans were left awaiting official confirmation from the ceremony.
briefs.bodyText:
With the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony underway in London, football fans thought they had discovered the winner before the trophy was even presented, after the award’s official website appeared to publish an article declaring 
Harry Kane
 the champion. The excitement quickly turned into confusion when similar articles emerged for Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal, leaving supporters wondering whether the result had been leaked or the organisers had simply prepared their announcements in advance.
Harry Kane appears to have won the Ballon d’Or
The Bayern Munich striker initially appeared to have received the biggest individual prize in football after an article titled “Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season” surfaced on the official website. Screenshots spread rapidly across social media, where English supporters began celebrating the apparent confirmation of Kane’s victory.
Kane entered the ceremony among the leading contenders after an extraordinary season, with reports highlighting his 73 goals for club and country, although the leaked article referenced a 61-goal season.
Mbappe and Yamal articles deepen the confusion
The apparent leak soon became less convincing when articles declaring Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal winners also appeared on the Ballon d’Or website.
One headline read, “Kylian Mbappé wins 2026 Ballon d’Or for consistency personified at the very highest level,” while another declared, “Lamine Yamal wins the 2026 Ballon d’Or and sets an unprecedented record!” The pages were reportedly prepared in advance for the possibility of any of the three leading candidates being announced on stage, rather than confirming the actual result.
The website subsequently removed the page, while the appearance of all three articles left fans without any reliable indication of who would receive the award.
Yamal, Kane and Mbappe had emerged as the leading candidates after outstanding campaigns, with Yamal winning the World Cup with Spain and La Liga with Barcelona, Kane spearheading Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga title and England’s run to the North American World Cup semi-finals, and Mbappe becoming the World Cup’s all-time leading goalscorer while claiming the 2026 Golden Boot.
Ballon d’Or countdown continues in London
The ceremony is taking place at the London Palladium Theatre, with the main event scheduled to begin at 8pm GMT on Monday, October 26, corresponding to 1.30am IST on Tuesday, October 27.
France Football has already begun revealing the lower positions, counting down from 30th to 11th in both the men’s and women’s rankings before the final ten are unveiled individually on stage. The countdown will continue until the leading candidates remain and the official winners are announced, meaning the website’s prematurely published articles have offered no confirmed answer.
